articleTitle: Modified FkP for Categorical Data Clustering and Its Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Many scientific communities have used Categorical data clustering to classify objects in large databases. A fuzzy k-partition (Fkp) approach has been proposed for categorical data clustering to classify the objects. However, existing Fuzzy k-partition approaches have a long execution time and low clustering accuracy. Furthermore, in the Fuzzy k-partition approach, the parameter maximizes the classification likelihood function for the same categories, producing the same results. To address these issues, we propose a k-partition based on Soft Sets. Categorical data can be classified using the soft sets parameterization tools. The proposed approach differs from previous approaches in that it is based on soft sets rather than the likelihood function of multivariate multinomial distributions. The experiments are conducted on the UCI dataset. The result shows that the proposed achieves better performance in terms of purity and time response.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Reviews on Ijen Crater Using the Naive Bayes Classifier Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Ijen Crater is one of the tourist attractions in Banyuwangi Regency in East Java Province which has an attraction for local and foreign tourists. Many comments from the public or visitors from outside the region regarding the Ij en Crater tourist attraction can be analyzed using sentiment analysis. The author uses the Naïve Bayes Classifier algorithm with TF-IDF feature extraction in analyzing the sentiment. The author used comment data that scrapped from TripAdvisor's social media to select the Ij en Crater tourist attraction with 1285 comment data. The data will be classified with positive, negative, and neutral labels using NLP and experts. The aim of this research is to analyze trends in public and visitor sentiment towards the Ijen Crater object. From the results of this research, it was found that public and visitor sentiment tended to be positive, namely 83.4% with the TF-IDF feature selection. Furthermore, This study has not implemented data balancing, as is known that in this study the number of each positive, negative and neutral class has a very varied number with a wide range of values.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of the Impact of Dataset Size on Classification Performance in the Cognitive Bloom's Taxonomy
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The dataset of questions in the Cognitive Bloom's Taxonomy (BT) classification case uses a lot of private datasets. The lack of public datasets leads to a lack of performance comparison in the classification model. This study aims to determine the impact of the dataset performance model on the performance of the classification model. The classification model uses a classification algorithm model with optimization in feature extraction and feature selection on cognitive BT, including Naïve Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF) on three public datasets. Three groups of datasets were used: small, medium, and large. The evaluation technique uses precision, accuracy, recall, specificity, and f1-score metrics and tests performance stability with k-fold cross-validation. The result of the study is that the overall classifier's performance depends on The degree of accuracy with which the dataset represents the original distribution relative to its size. The accuracy can be improved by adding extraction and selection features. The statistically tested datasets have significant differences between the models. The Tukey HSD test shows that the differences between the models have significant values.

articleTitle: Multiclass Cyberbullying Detection Using BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: On social media, cyberbullying has grown into a significant issue that impacts people's mental health and well-being. As the language used is often subtle and implicit, it is difficult to detect cyberbullying directly. This study examines the efficacy of transformer-based models, specifically BERT and DistilBERT, to detect cyberbullying compared to conventional machine learning techniques using TF-IDF with Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Random Forest. To improve the accuracy of the model, we preprocessed the data by normalizing the text, removing stopwords, and expanding slang. Although DistilBERT achieves a competitive 94% accuracy with less computational requirements, the experimental results show that BERT surpasses the standard model with 95% accuracy, 95% precision, 95% recall, and an Fl-score of 95%. The results show that transformer models - particularly BERT - are more effective than conventional methods in capturing the nuanced context of coarse language. This research highlights the potential of transformers for accurate cyberbullying detection on social media, with future research aiming to optimize model efficiency and explore ensemble methods to further improve performance.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network for Sentiment Analysis of Indonesian Online News
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The development of online news has made it the primary source of information for the public, replacing the previously dominant position of print media. In increasingly fierce competition, many media companies rely on page views to drive advertising revenue, making it one of their key performance indicators. By utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), companies can extract sentiment from news headlines. The results of sentiment analysis predictions from online news headlines can be used to determine the proportion of popular news based on page views. This allows us to identify whether popular news (news with high page views) comes from negative or positive headlines. This information can be utilized by media outlets to create more engaging headlines to increase the number of popular news articles. By optimizing CNN parameters during training, the accuracy of the testing model can be enhanced. The results of this research show that sentiment analysis with Convolutional Neural Network shows the best accuracy result of 76.94% when using 100 filters and a filter size of 5. Positive news headlines are more likely to result in popular news compared to negative headlines

articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Machine Learning Techniques: Dealing with Imbalanced Data using Over-Sampling and Under-Sampling Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Digital banking has eased financial transactions and significantly increased fraudulent activities. Credit card companies must identify fraudulent transactions to prevent customers from being charged for unauthorized purchases. Previously, several machine-learning methodologies and classifiers have been employed to identify fraudulent transactions. Nonetheless, due to the constantly evolving nature of fraud patterns, it is essential to examine new frauds and formulate a model based on these new patterns. Furthermore, authentic transactions are frequently higher than fraudulent ones, making it very difficult to distinguish between them. This issue must be addressed urgently to detect these fraudulent activities as they occur and notify the right individuals. This research proposes using machine learning techniques to identify and report fraudulent transactions automatically. We mainly address the class imbalance problem (fraud and non-fraud) by evaluating outcomes from several over-sampling and under-sampling methods. Several sampling techniques have been applied to the training set. However, SMOTE and ROS+RUS have been selected based on better precision and recall of the training data. Machine learning models can produce precise predictions and learn from a more balanced distribution. A performance comparison of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and ensemble learning using test data is performed, and the comparison is made with baseline models, including Random Forest and XGBoost.

articleTitle: Automating Embryo Quality Classification in IVF by Comparing the Performance of ResNet50, VGG16, and InceptionV3
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Infertility affects millions of couples worldwide, and the success of In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) heavily depends on accurate assessment of embryo quality, which is currently performed manually and is prone to subjectivity. This study investigates the use of deep learning for automating embryo classification based on microscopic images from Day 3 and Day 5 of development. Four models ResNet50, VGG16, InceptionV3, and a custom CNN were trained on 1,432 images (1,076 from Day 3 and 356 from Day 5) using the Adam optimizer at a learning rate of 0.0001 for 100 epochs. Results show InceptionV3 achieving the highest accuracy on Day 3 (99.09%) and Day 5 (89.5%), with precision, recall, and F1-scores all at 0.99 and 0.89, respectively. ResNet50 followed closely with Day 3 accuracy of 97.27% and Day 5 accuracy of 86.8%. The custom CNN demonstrated moderate performance, achieving 91.82% accuracy on Day 3 and 81.6% on Day 5, while VGG16 showed the lowest performance. These findings highlight InceptionV3 as the most reliable model, while the custom CNN offers practical solutions for smaller datasets or computationally constrained environments. This approach enhances IVF precision and efficiency, minimizing subjectivity and accelerating analysis.

articleTitle: Comparison of Clustering Techniques for Vessel Sailing Pattern Utilizing Space-Based AIS Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The analysis of vessel sailing patterns is crucial for enhancing maritime safety and navigation efficiency. This study compares the performance of K-Means and DBSCAN clustering techniques in analyzing vessel movements using space-based Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from the LAPAN-A2 and LAPAN-A3 satellites, focusing on eastern Indonesian waters. Vessel stability is assessed through the standard deviation of Speed Over Ground (SOG) and Course Over Ground (COG). The AIS data is normalized using Min-Max scaling and analyzed with both K-Means and DBSCAN algorithms. Performance is measured using the Silhouette Score and the Calinski-Harabasz Index to evaluate cluster quality. Results show that K-Means achieves a Silhouette Score of 0.552 and a Calinski-Harabasz Index of 814.846, identifying stable movement patterns in well-defined clusters. Conversely, DBSCAN achieves a higher Silhouette Score of 0.731, better detecting anomalies and noise, though with a lower Calinski-Harabasz Index of 361.665. This comparative analysis underscores the complementary strengths of each method, offering valuable insights for maritime authorities in improving navigational safety and operational efficiency through advanced data analytics.

articleTitle: Monocular 3D Object Detection for Robotics
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: 3D object detection is considered as computationally expensive problem as it heavily relies on processing extensive sensory data making it unsuitable for the real-time application. To address this problem, we propose a monocular 3D object detection method for robotics, particularly the autonomous vehicles, using the YOLOv3 algorithm, known for its efficiency and speed. To evaluate the performance of the proposed approach, we used KITTI dataset, one of the most robust 3D object detection datasets. The proposed approach is computationally less expensive, suitable for real-time applications, and highly accurate. Our approach utilizes the Darknet53 backbone network with 74 convolutional layers along with the YOLOv3. We have extensively evaluated the proposed approach where each object class has a custom mAP evaluation script 0.5 IoU for the evaluation process and mAP results. The best outcome, namely a mAP value of 0.60, was obtained after several training processes. The result showed that YOLOv3 is one of the key candidates for the monocular 3D object detection.

articleTitle: An IoT-Driven Fuzzy Decision Model for Determining Room Comfort
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The use of the Internet of Things (IoT) has been widely adopted for a lot of purposes. Business process automation is one type of implementation that has been carried out. In addition, the data successfully captured by the IoT ecosystem can be utilized for various computer modeling needs, including the decision model construction in assessing room quality. The decision model itself is a computer model supporting the decision maker in decision making process. This research, via four simple research stages, aims to develop an IoT-based decision model to evaluate room quality based on two parameters: temperature and humidity. The design of the IoT environment and the implementation of temperature and humidity data readings in a room are used as input data for a decision model to assess the comfort level of the room. In this study, the primary method used to design the model is object-oriented, while fuzzy logic is employed to build the model. The developed decision model can simulate data captured from the designed IoT ecosystem, successfully assessing the comfort level of a room. From the simulation results using 18 data points (from 9 days of data capturing) captured by temperature and humidity sensors, the average comfort level of the room was found to be 19.7873.

articleTitle: Evaluation of NASA POWER and ERA5 for Estimating Solar Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Solar radiation is a weather parameter that has an essential role in climate, meteorology, and renewable energy. In the field of renewable energy, solar radiation data is used to design and optimize solar panel systems, thereby increasing efficiency and energy output. In meteorology and climate, solar radiation data plays a role in climate modelling for climate change analysis and weather prediction. Solar radiation can be observed in two methods such as ground-based monitoring and satellite data monitoring. Ground-based monitoring uses Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) and solar radiation observations are made through satellites orbiting the earth, such as NASA Power and ERA5 Reanalysis Dataset. The advantages of satellite observations are that they can reach a wide spatial area but lack precision, while ground-based observations have high accuracy but low spatial coverage. This study evaluates quality of solar radiation in ERA5 and NASA Power to solar radiation of pyranometer sensor in AWS. The results show that NASA Power has solar radiation modeling that tends to underestimate AWS, in coefficient of determination of 0.52, RMSE and ME of 248.23 W/M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 318.00 W/M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, while ERA5 shows better accuracy with a coefficient of determination of 0.78 and RMSE and ME of 199.42 W/M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 245.99 W/M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The quality of solar radiation estimates produced by ERA5 and NASA Power is influenced by the spatial resolution of each modeling.

articleTitle: Meet-in-the-Middle Attacks on 2-GOST with Four Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Double encryption, particularly through the 2-GOST method, is expected to enhance security. For instance, in the case of 2-GOST, a brute-force attack would require testing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{256}\times \mathrm{a}^{256}$</tex> possible keys. However, this level of security is not always guaranteed due to the potential for Meet-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks using four scenarios. The MITM approach splits the key search process into two stages, which are then compared. In this study, four scenarios were applied using 100,000 samples, assuming <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{2}$</tex> fall within this range. The results showed that the MITM attack with four scenarios on 2-GOST reduced the computational time from 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">512</sup> to 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">257</sup>. This examination also provides an analysis of the vulnerabilities of the 2-GOST scheme to MITM attacks and discusses the potential defenses and countermeasures against these attacks.

articleTitle: Generating Question Using Retrieval Augmented Generation with Large Language Model: Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Rapid technological developments affect all aspects of life, especially in the field of education. One application of technology in the field of education is the automatic creation of questions. Automatic creation of questions is proposed by the author using the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) method with Large Language Model (LLM). The aim is to help teachers in creating automatic exam questions by generating questions in the question bank or question database with the difficulty level of the questions. The author uses 3 test scenarios, namely ideal conditions, non-ideal conditions and slightly ideal conditions using 3 models, such as Llama 3, Cohere LLM and GPT 2. The author's goal in using 3 models is to compare models seen from the results of their accuracy. The results of the experiments conducted are that in ideal conditions, Llama-3-8B and GPT 2 get a very good accuracy score of 100%, while Cohere LLM gets an accuracy score of 80%. In non-ideal conditions, Cohere LLM gets the best score among other models. Cohere LLM gets an accuracy score of 80%, while Llama-3-8B and GPT 2 get an accuracy score of 67%. In slightly ideal conditions, Llama-3-8B gets the highest accuracy score of 100%. Cohere LLM and GPT 2 get a poor score of 67%. From these results, it can be concluded that Llama-3-8B is the best model compared to the other 2 models in generating questions. Then followed by GPT 2 and Cohere LLM

articleTitle: Performance of Naive Bayes Algorithm on Extreme Rainfall Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Accurate rainfall prediction is important for disaster mitigation, water management, and agricultural planning. Particularly, in areas with extreme monthly rainfall variations like Malang Regency, future weather prediction is a critical need. Classification of rainfall data could be considered to process information into valuable knowledge for the benefit of many people. This research utilized the Naive Bayes algorithm for classification, implemented within RapidMiner, using datasets from the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) collected over a one-year period, from January 2021 to February 2022. Several stages were needed to determine changes in rainfall patterns, consisting of data collection, understanding, preparation, modeling, evaluation, and dissemination. The dataset includes four parameters: average temperature, humidity, maximum wind speed, and wind direction. Three training and test data scenarios were implemented to optimize model performance. The study demonstrates that the Naive Bayes algorithm within RapidMiner effectively predicts rainfall categories, including light, medium, or heavy rainfall, with a maximum accuracy of 85.71%, making it a reliable tool for classifying rainfall intensity.

articleTitle: Algorithm Adaptation Methods for Prediction of Opinion and Exceptions in Financial Statements Audit Reports: Case for Financial Statements Audit in Riau Islands Province
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)

authors.preferredName: Thio Marta Elisa Yuridis Butar Butar

abstract: Prior research on financial statement audits has mostly employed multi-label classification, like the Problem Transformation Methods, and single-label classification, such as opinion prediction, identification, and detection. Using information from financial statement audit reports in the Riau Islands province, we suggest applying multi-label classification to predict “opinion and exceptions.” We employ opinion and exceptions as labels and financial ratios as attributes. Back-Propagation Neural Network (BPNN) and Deep Back-Propagation Neural Network (DBPNN), two Algorithm Adaptation Methods, are employed in this study. Two Algorithm Adaptation Methods are computed using two model architectures, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Voted Perceptron (VP). For Hamming Loss (HL), One Error (OE), Rank Loss (RL), and Average Precision (AP), the best evaluation metric outcomes are 0.0417, 0.0000, 0.0333, and 0.9786, respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of IEC 61850 Protocol Automation System at the Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research aims to improve the power quality of the electrical system by installing a single-tuned passive filter, focusing on reducing high harmonic distortion. Before the installation of the filter, the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the system measured 49.84%, above the standard permissible limit. After applying the single-tuned passive filter, the measurement results showed a significant reduction in THD to 2.79%, which complies with the IEEE 519–2014 standard. This reduction in harmonic distortion contributes to improving system operating efficiency and extending the life of the connected equipment. In order to ensure continuous power quality, harmonics monitoring measures will be implemented using the IEC 61850 communication protocol. This protocol enables the integration of real-time and standardized monitoring systems, facilitating effective monitoring and analysis of harmonics. With these significant results, using single-tuned passive filters proved to be an efficient solution for harmonic reduction. At the same time, the IEC 61850 protocol is expected to provide accurate and integrated monitoring capabilities to ensure power quality is maintained in the future.

articleTitle: Design of Soil Fertility Detection System Using Fuzzy Mamdani Method based on GIS Site Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Soil fertility is a critical factor in agricultural productivity, influencing crop yields and the overall sustainability of farming practices. This research paper proposes a soil fertility detection system using Fuzzy Mamdani method integrated with Geographic Information System (GIS) site mapping. The proposed system aims to provide precise and automated soil fertility analysis by considering various soil parameters such as temperature, moisture and PH. As an initial stage of the research, soil fertility detection is modeled using Matlab software and compared with manual calculations. The test results on the soil temperature sensor obtained MAPE of 3.54639, the soil moisture sensor obtained MAPE of 1.371602 and the soil PH sensor obtained MAPE of 3.282293. The mapping accuracy test results showed an average distance difference of 0.0016585 centimeter between the device's coordinates and Google Maps coordinates. The soil fertility detection modelling results between the Matlab simulation and manual calculations obtained an error of 0.466%.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Decision Support System for Real-Time Vehicle Maintenance Scheduling in the Fourth Industrial Revolution
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) has transformed manufacturing and maintenance through advanced technologies, including the Internet of Things (IoT), cloud computing, and Decision Support Systems (DSS). In vehicle maintenance, IoT enables real-time data collection from Electronic Control Units to facilitate predictive and periodic maintenance, enhancing reliability and efficiency. This study develops an IoT-based DSS for periodic vehicle maintenance, focusing on data from vehicle sensors to optimize maintenance intervals based on mileage and component conditions. The system was designed using a web server and database infrastructure, integrated with Application Programming Interfaces to enable real-time communication between the vehicle's sensors and a web dashboard. The dashboard displays component statuses and provides maintenance recommendations. Testing involved function and performance evaluations on data communication between an OBD-II scanner, IoT gateway, and web dashboard. The system reads real-time vehicle data effectively, provides maintenance recommendations based on pre-set DSS rules, and updates component status on the web interface. Tests confirmed synchronization between sensor readings and displayed data, with a response delay under 500 ms, meeting real-time system criteria. The IoT-based DSS for vehicle maintenance proved effective in automating maintenance scheduling, providing users with timely and accurate recommendations. This system promotes efficient and proactive vehicle maintenance, aligning with 4IR goals by enhancing operational reliability through real-time data integration and automated decision support.

articleTitle: Modified YoloV10x for Object Detection on Drone-based Image Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Images captured by an AI-powered drone are often used for various purposes, including object detection. However, detecting small objects remains challenging in drone-captured images, requiring a reliable deep-learning architecture to handle feature extraction and image downsampling during the machine-learning process. This research aims to propose a deep-learning architecture to tackle such challenges. Based on the YoloV10x architecture, the conditional identity blocks in the backbone part are replaced by convolution and bottleneck blocks for faster and more efficient downsampling. Using the VISDRONE DET dataset, the learning process was performed from scratch. The model's performance evaluation uses mean Average Precision (mAP) and loss functions. Compared to the baseline architecture called Realtime Detection Transformer (RT-DETR), the proposed architecture can increase by approx-imately an average of 27% mAP scores for each class in the dataset.

articleTitle: Monthly Forecasting Indonesian Coffee Production Using Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Indonesia, a major global coffee producer, encounters significant seasonal and annual fluctuations in coffee production attributable to various factors including climate, economic conditions, and agricultural practices. Precise forecasting of monthly coffee production is essential for stakeholders throughout the supply chain, facilitating planning, resource distribution, and market stability. This study examines the utilization of the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) model for monthly predictions of Indonesian coffee production. The ELM model is trained and evaluated using data from 2014 to 2023, employing different train-test splits to measure its predictive efficacy. The results demonstrate that the ELM model effectively captures overall production trends, with the optimal configuration attained at an 80–20 train-test split, resulting in a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 8,144.66 tons. The number of neurons is 1500 and the iterations value is 2000. This model showed a promising result. Nevertheless, elevated error rates are noted in larger test splits, underscoring possible constraints in model generalization with restricted data. The analysis indicates that incorporating supplementary variables, including climatic and economic factors, along with more detailed data, may improve model precision. This study illustrates the efficacy of ELM in predicting coffee production and offers insights into model enhancements for agricultural forecasting applications.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Assessment of SCADA Installation Case Study: PT PLN UID Jakarta Raya
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: PT PLN UID Jakarta, as the electricity provider in Jakarta, needs to determine the number of SCADA installations so that the investment costs incurred are proportional to the benefits obtained. This paper compares three parameters, which are SAIDI, cost, and economic benefit to determine the optimum number of SCADA facilities that should be added to the distribution substation. The result of this paper shows that SCADA can reduce SAIDI, but not in a linear manner. The increase in economic benefits gained is also not always proportional to the investment costs. There is an optimal point where adding SCADA at that number of distribution substations is the last addition that provides a reduction in SAIDI and an increase in economic benefit proportional to the costs.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis on Cyber Attacks Against Bank Syariah Indonesia Using the IndoBERT Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Bank Syariah Indonesia is one of the Islamic banks that has obtained an operational license from the National Sharia Council. The development and utilization of information technology carries its own risks for the banking sector. Like the ransomware attack experienced by Bank Syariah Indonesia on May 8–11, 2023, the perpetrators claimed to have stolen 15 million customer data, employee information, and around 1.5 terabytes of internal data. This incident triggered various responses from the public on social media, one of which was on Twitter, through uploads known as tweets. This study aims to analyze Twitter sentiment towards the cyber attack that occurred at BSI to determine the majority of public sentiment categories towards the incident. The results of the study showed that the majority of sentiment was negative sentiment as many as 13,120 tweets or 58.4% of the total sentiment. Testing in this study showed that the IndoBERT model had good performance in classifying sentiment classes with an accuracy value of 93%, precision of 91%, recall of 90%, and F1-Score of 90%.

articleTitle: Shrimps Classification Optimization Using Modified CNN-VGG16
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Vannamei shrimp is the ideal product choice to support food security, offering a range of unparalleled advantages. To ensure a good quality and quantity of vannamei shrimp harvest, feed management must be of the highest standard. It is crucial to provide the shrimp with the optimal amount of feed to ensure their development and growth. However, excessive feeding will also result in higher production costs and waste accumulation in the pond. Monitoring the accuracy of feeding is essential. The development of shrimp growth must be observed using image processing. We obtain shrimp size by classifying shrimp samples using the CNN-VGG16 method. The image is captured by placing the webcam perpendicular to the position of the shrimp. Each sample is taken with 1000 data points, with five sample variations representing five different shrimp sizes. A notable disadvantage of the CNN-VGG16 algorithm is the relatively large number of parameters, necessitating modification of the CNN-VGG16 structure to enhance efficiency. The test results are excellent, with a loss value of 0.07680364698171616 and an accuracy value of 0.976047933101654.

articleTitle: Reducing Class Imbalance with Undersampling for Improvement of Classification Method in Liver Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: One dataset with a class imbalance is the liver disease dataset, where the liver class has 406 instances, while the non-liver class has only 164 instances. This imbalance causes machine learning methods, especially classification methods, to tend to classify the majority class (liver) and ignore the minority class (non-liver). In this situation, machine learning models may achieve high accuracy simply by predicting the majority class, which does not reflect their true ability to detect the disease accurately. Therefore, this study aims to improve the performance of Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest methods in classifying liver disease by addressing data imbalance through under-sampling approaches. The study uses SVM and Random Forest as classification methods, while to handle data imbalance in the liver disease dataset, the study uses under-sampling methods such as Random Under-sampling (RUS) and Edited Nearest Neighbors (ENN). The research results show that the SVM method with ENN produces a better AUC value than RUS and without under-sampling, with a value of 78.8%. Meanwhile, Random Forest with ENN achieved a higher AUC than RUS and without under-sampling, reaching 84.3%. These findings prove that the under-sampling approach can improve the AUC value of SVM and Random Forest methods compared to not using under-sampling. Moreover, ENN proves to be superior to RUS, and there is no under-sampling in both classification algorithms used.

articleTitle: Serverless Computing Model Using Kubernetes and Knative in a Scalable Cloud Development
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: With the advancement of technology, more organizations are transitioning to Cloud Computing to meet their infrastructure needs. The popularity of this technology can be attributed to its numerous advantages, including cost-effectiveness and scalability. One focus of Cloud Computing is Serverless Computing, which provides a usage-based system allowing users to allocate costs only for the resources used, thereby enhancing cost efficiency and resource utilization. The open-source Knative Framework project was developed to adopt Serverless computing, adding components to Kubernetes to build a Serverless system. Using the Knative Framework, users can implement serverless services without relying on other cloud providers. This research aims to implement a Serverless system using Knative and conduct performance testing with parameters such as response time, resource utilization, and failure rates. The research results in a functioning Serverless system alongside Kubernetes and a usable monitoring system. It is found that the resource utilization performance of serverless CPU and RAM is similar to that of conventional systems. Additionally, the Cold Start time for the Serverless system is found to be 2.28 seconds. The Serverless system successfully performs automatic scaling based on incoming traffic demand.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Foot-Operated Hierarchical Character Selection Keyboard for Individuals with Upper Limb Disabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research was designed to present a foot-operated assistive keyboard for people with hand disabilities, enabling them to access computers and type efficiently. It consists of five buttons-four to select options and one to cancel-along with an OLED display that guides users through a hierarchical character selection menu. In an evaluation involving five participants typing six sentences in their national language, the QWERTY keyboard was the most efficient, with typing times between 13.49 and 27.84 seconds, followed by the T9 keyboard with times ranging from 62.42 to 130.36 seconds. The proposed keyboard, specifically designed for accessibility with only four foot-operated buttons, had the longest typing times, between 218.68 and 450.60 seconds. While slower, the device reduces physical and cognitive effort, with the potential to improve further with user feedback and technological refinements. This study highlighted the importance of open-source customization in developing accessible assistive tools.

articleTitle: Predicting Machine Learning for Early Diabetes Mellitus Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is characterized by hyperglycemia, a chronic illness caused by inadequate insulin synthesis or an abnormal insulin response. Early identification is crucial since the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) anticipate that by 2060, the number of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) cases among those under 20 would have skyrocketed by 700%. This article offers a thorough approach to diabetes prediction using three datasets: the Pima Indian Diabetes Dataset, the Iraqi Diabetes Dataset, and a medical dataset from Kaggle. Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, SVM, K-Nearest Neighbours, Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting, and many neural network designs (two-layered neural networks, LSTM, and Bi-LSTM) were among the machine learning models used, along with a voting classifier. The experimental findings demonstrate that machine learning can improve diabetes diagnosis and treatment by demonstrating robust prediction capabilities across models.

articleTitle: Yolov10-Based Student Activity Identification as Personalization of Appropriate Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Suitable learning methods can significantly improve the quality and learning outcomes of students. An independent curriculum personalizes learning methods to create an inclusive and student centred learning environment. This approach can be done through the Student-Centered Learning (SCL) method. However, most of the literature states that these efforts are only done by exploration using manual methods. That shows that there are limitations in the approach used so far. Therefore, this research focuses on the automatic detection of student learning activity engagement in the classroom. We implemented the You Only Looks Once version 10 Medium (YOLOv10-M) algorithm that has been trained using a specific dataset. Based on the training results, the model can recognize visual behaviors based on student engagement during classroom learning activities. The dataset used is 8,884 total images with 8 classes. The experimental results of the model produced excellent detection performance with an average precision (mAP@50) of 91.1%. The model is proven to have the potential to help teachers recognize students' learning activities in real-time in classrooms as an evaluation of learning methods and constructional adjustments.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Design Approach to Detect Malicious Injections in Government Websites: Combating Hidden Online Gambling Pages
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The increasing case of online gambling activities in Indonesia requires the government, particularly through the Ministry of Communication and Digital (Komdigi), to pay special attention to addressing this issue. Komdigi has actively conducted outreach programs about the dangers of online gambling from various aspects of life. Additionally, thousands of websites suspected of hosting online gambling activities have been blocked. However, many security vulnerabilities remain in government-owned web applications, making them vulnerable to hacker attacks, such as illegal hidden online gambling page injection into these websites. Therefore, this study developed a method to prevent hackers from performing injections or upload unwanted hidden online gambling page using a Bash script that leverages the lnotify(); function feature available in Linux operating systems. This Bash script is designed to be lightweight, minimizing the use of resources such as CPU and server memory. This approach enables quick detection and send notification to suspicious activities without disrupting the server's primary performance, making it a suitable solution for implementation in government infrastructures that often face resource constraints.

articleTitle: Pretrained Deep CNN Model Evaluation for Brain Stroke Detection Using CT Scan Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Stroke is one of the primary medical conditions worldwide, occurring when blood flow to the brain is interrupted, representing a significant challenge in global healthcare. The rising global burden of stroke underscores the essential role of examining accurate diagnostic methods to improve patient outcomes. Despite advances in medical imaging and computational techniques, maintaining high accuracy in stroke detection remains crucial to optimize diagnostic results, enabling timely and appropriate patient care. This study is dedicated to evaluating pretrained models based on convolutional neural network architectures, including Xception, VGG16, VGG19, InceptionV3, and InceptionResNetV2, and their applications in neurological stroke diagnosis using computed tomography (CT) scans. Leveraging transfer learning and fine-tuning techniques, this study achieves significant improvements in stroke detection accuracy. Notably, the VGG16 and VGG19 models demonstrate excellent performance, with accuracy rates increasing from 92.000% (during transfer learning) to 97.200% (after fine-tuning). These empirical results confirm the effectiveness of deep learning methods in enhancing stroke detection accuracy, thus helping to close the gap between current and more precise diagnostic approaches in stroke management. The obtained data provide a strong foundation for considering deep learning models in stroke recognition processes, with the potential to improve patient care quality and alleviate the burden on healthcare services.

articleTitle: Cheating Detection in System Computer-Based Test (CBT) Based on Participant's Facial Images using PCA Feature Reduction on CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Covid-19 has caused whole world to implementing online learning to prevent mass gatherings in one place. By conducting online learning, exams also running with online method. Before pandemic covid-19 cheating during exams was already become problem in evaluating the result of learning and with pandemic, controls to prevent cheating are urgently needed. Cheating during exam with computer-based test (CBT) become problem, this is challenge for artificial intelligence in detecting cheating during exams based on participant's face. This paper presenting a comparison model Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and model CNN with reduction Principal Component Analysis (PCA) in detection cheating during exams. The dataset that uses to training and testing with the CNN architecture that was built provides 77% accuracy. By adding PCA reduction to feature CNN, the accuracy increases to 83% with same training and testing data. Form this case we can conclude that using PCA in reducing CNN features can increase model performance.

articleTitle: Electronic Warfare Frequency Hopping for Radar Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research focuses on the implementation of frequency agility techniques specifically frequency hopping in radar systems, particularly in the context of electronic warfare. The study investigates the use of phased array radar to detect approaching aircraft equipped with jammers capable of intercepting and spoofing radar signals. The radar system is designed to transmit waveforms with different operating frequencies to counter the effects of jamming. The research includes the development of a Simulink model to simulate the radar system, incorporating blocks for waveform generation, signal propagation, and signal processing. The model allows for the analysis of how radar and jammer signals interact and gain advantage over each other. Key components of the model include a jammer block that generates jamming signals based on incoming radar signals, and signal processing blocks for filtering and extracting radar signals from different frequency bands. Overall, the research aims to provide insights into the effectiveness of frequency hopping and frequency agility techniques in mitigating jamming effects in radar systems, with potential applications in electronic warfare and radar signal processing.

articleTitle: Analysis of 5G New Radio Network Planning with 2300 MHz Frequency in Balikpapan City
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This study aims to provide initial guidance for implementing 5G New Radio (NR) technology in Indonesia, specifically in Balikpapan. It focuses on planning a 5G NR network for a 2300 MHz frequency, covering a total area of 511.01 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the city. This is a strategic step to strengthen the position of Balikpapan city as the center of coal export industry in East Kalimantan. The propagation model used is for 5G NR Urban Macro (UMa) for 5G NR which is standardized by 3GPP TR 38.900. The results of this plan are simulated using Atoll Software and produce a pathloss value of 110.4824905 dB, a coverage radius of 1181.08m. 73 sites are required to set up a good network service. From the downlink simulation results, the SS-RSRP parameter is displayed with an average value of -71.02 dBm, then the SS-SINR parameter simulation results with an average value of 29.31 dB, and the last is the throughput parameter with an average value of 255 Mbps.

articleTitle: Gaussian Filter Optimization for Segmentation Retinal Fundus Images in Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy alludes to a boundary that takes put in diabetes mellitus harming the blood vessel arranged display within the retina. This may imperil the subject's vision if they have diabetes. It can take a little time to perform a DR determination utilizing color fundus pictures since experienced clinicians are required to identify the tumors within the symbolism utilized to distinguish the sickness. This research using 3669 data were collage using open data. CNN are also highly successful at classifying pictures when connected within the display circumstance, especially compared to the high quality and usefulness strategies utilized. To guarantee high results, it needs a cutting-edge CNN show that might decide the characteristics of the fundus pictures. The implementation of the Gaussian filter result image on the identification performance gets the highest accuracy from the 3×3 structural element is 77%. Its shown that algorithm is feasible. The investigation's discoveries that the approach performed way better than elective approaches and can identify the specifics of an image as a health industry option for early detection of disease.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Arabica Coffee Beans Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Coffee has an important role in the international economy. One-of-a-kind coffee which is often enjoyed is Arabica. To drink coffee in Indonesia has become a trend in any circles. The problems appear when arabica coffee undergoes various processes. At first glance it looks the same because it comes from the Arabica coffee type. Classifying coffee types manually requires time and human effort which can be seen directly by the eye. However, this is less than optimal because it allows for human error. Many studies discuss the classification of coffee beans using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method. But previous researchers did not discuss loss and time effectiveness. The data set used is Arabica coffee images using labels, namely inculant, anaerobic and classic with a total of 300 coffee bean images which are divided into training data and test data with a ratio of 80:20. The accuracy value of the CNN Alexnet 4096 method was obtained at 94% at the 200th epoch with a learning rate of 0.0001.

articleTitle: Smart Validation of Student Registration Documents Using CNNs with Hyperparameter Tuning and Data Augmentation: A Case Study in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Efficient and accurate validation of student registration documents is critical for higher education institutions, yet traditional manual methods are increasingly inadequate for handling large-scale admissions. This study presents a novel application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) combined with advanced hyperparameter tuning and data augmentation techniques to automate the validation process. By fine-tuning hyperparameters using Grid Search and augmenting the dataset with context-specific transformations, the proposed model achieves a significant accuracy improvement. Trained on 500 document images, our approach demonstrates superior performance, achieving 97% accuracy for birth certificates, 88% for diplomas, 88% for family cards, 84% for identity cards, and 94% for exam result certificates, resulting in an overall accuracy of 91.1%. This research not only offers an innovative solution to the challenges of document validation in university admissions but also provides a scalable framework applicable across various domains. The deployment of this model in a real-time system further highlights its practical implications, setting a new benchmark in the field of educational administration.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Drip Irrigation System Real-Time Emission Uniformity (REU) Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research aims to develop a model for recording and measuring real-time emission uniformity (REU) in a drip irrigation system. Internet of Things (IoT) technology is employed, integrating multiple sensors with a microcontroller to capture data on pressure, discharge, and water volume. These parameters serve as input data for the model to ascertain the percentage of emissions uniformity (EU). A comparison was conducted between the created model REU and manual measurement model EU to evaluate accuracy. Analysis of 13 comparisons indicated that the REU results approximated the EU standard, with MSE value of 1.26 and RMSE value of 1,12. This method provides a more efficient irrigation solution and may be further refined to ensure more consistent water distribution, hence promoting sustainable and resource-efficient farming practices.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Control System of TDS Levels in AB Mix Nutrition in Vertical Hydroponic Photovoltaic for Pakcoy Plant Growth
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Hydroponics is an agricultural cultivation system that does not use soil; instead, the soil medium is replaced with water containing nutrients. Hydroponics is used for farming in limited spaces and without soil. This method can help increase food production. The hydroponic system is currently being developed to address issues affecting plant growth by automatically controlling growth parameters, which can maximize crop yields and minimize failures. One effort to maintain hydroponic quality is by monitoring the nutrient content in the hydroponic system, specifically by maintaining the nutrient levels. This monitoring uses the Internet of Things (IoT), which can be accessed via smartphones, allowing for remote monitoring. Additionally, the hydroponic system uses photovoltaic technology so that hydroponics can be developed even in areas far from electrical sources. With the vertical hydroponic nutrient content monitoring system, it is expected to improve the quality of crop production. Research results show that the growth of pakcoy plants with control is better compared to without control, as seen from the percentage of height growth and number of leaves. In terms of plant height growth, controlled pakcoy plants experienced a growth of 10.85%, while pakcoy plants without control showed a growth of 6.97%. The growth in the number of leaves of controlled pak choi plants showed a result of 10.90%, and the growth of leaves without control and monitoring showed a result of 5.71%.

articleTitle: Efficient Gunshot Scoring System with YOLOv8 Hole Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The implementation of an automatic gunshot scoring system is a necessary step to facilitate the assessment of gun shooting activities and enhance the performance of athletes. In the course of the gunshot scoring system, object detection based on YOLOv8 is employed to detect gunshot holes in shooting targets and automate a scoring process in shooting activities. This system is situated within the domain of computer vision, employing three lightweight YOLOv8 models. Three models are trained on a dataset comprising gunshot holes on a shooting sheet. Detection of gunshot holes provides location data of the object. The distance between the location of the gunshot hole and the center point of the shooting sheet is calculated and compared between score circles. The location of the gunshot hole concerning the scoring circle is used to determine the score value of the shot. The results show that YOLOv8 models have high accuracy in detecting gunshot holes and scoring systems. The best results are obtained by a small model exhibiting a precision value of 0.9921, a recall value of 0.9960, and an F1 score of 0.9941. In the context of real-time implementation, the nano model is the optimal choice for the YOLOv8 model, it exhibits a twofold reduction in inference time compared to the small model while maintaining a comparable level of accuracy.

articleTitle: The Impact of N-Grams on Classifying Final Project Documents Using Feature Extraction and K-Nearest Neighbors
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research aims to analyze the impact of n-gram usage on the classification of undergraduate theses of students in the Faculty of Engineering at Muhammadiyah University of Jember. In this study, the feature extraction and selection methods using n-grams are implemented alongside the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm to improve classification accuracy. The data used consists of thesis texts processed into feature representations using n-gram techniques. The feature selection process is conducted to choose the most significant features in determining the thesis category. The research results are expected to demonstrate that the use of n-grams as a feature extraction technique can significantly enhance the performance of KNN classification. Model performance evaluation is conducted using accuracy, precision, and recall metrics, indicating that the model with n-gram feature extraction and selection has higher accuracy compared to the model without n-grams.

articleTitle: Balancing Metrics Dynamic OSPF Optimizing Network Traffic in Sumatera
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Sumatera has a complex network topology with frequent network disruptions. A heavy traffic due to high internet. Congestion traffic in a network route caused by physical network's disruptions and limited bandwidth capacity in a route even though there are other routers could be flowed by load traffic. A router forwards packets to their destinations based on routing chosen by network operator. Static routing and dynamic routing are two type in network's routing. In this paper, we choose to discuss about dynamic routing using Interior Gateway Protocols. Open Short Path First or OSPF is most IGP using for traffic's network distribution with costing network's link named metric. However, with balancing metric OSPF, a traffic's route divided into paths headed to the same target router. In this paper, we discuss the proposed cost to update metrics in congestion network condition or optimizing any unbalance route based on the actual traffic's data. Actually, it takes times to update metrics without discover the formula. The proposed cost tries to transform an irregular cost existing in network into another equivalent set of metrics which targeted the same router. Numerical results in balancing metric OSPF reduce network congestion or unbalance route 80% in average in our troubleshooting experience compared with irregular metric cost. The limitation of using proposed cost due to the static traffic's eksisting remains in a route. Balancing route of the traffic's load provides best performance in the continuation of the telecommunications business.

articleTitle: An Automatic Nutrition Distribution and Disease Detection System for Hydroponic Spinach Plants Using IoT and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: In response to the increasing food demands driven by a growing human population and limited agricultural land, hydroponic farming has emerged as a solution for cultivating in confined spaces. Spinach is a valuable commodity among vegetables. It can be cultivated using hydroponics, but it is prone to diseases. Proper nutrient management based on the plants' needs is a crucial factor in the success of hydroponic farming. By using IoT technology, managing nutrients and detecting diseases in hydroponic spinach becomes more efficient compared to manual methods, which require time, effort, and specialized skills. This research aims to develop an automated system for managing nutrients and detecting diseases in hydroponic spinach using the nutrient film technique (NFT) and a Raspberry Pi as the control center. The system monitors pH, nutrient content, temperature, and humidity, as well as detects plant diseases. The disease detection is performed using a transfer learning architecture based on the MobileNetV2. The model was then integrated with the Blynk dashboard. The experiment results show that the temperature and humidity sensors, pH sensors, and nutrient sensors have an accuracy above 97% compared to manual tools. Meanwhile, the MobileNetV2 model has an accuracy of 57% in detecting diseases in spinach leaf images captured by a camera.

articleTitle: Design of Multiband Bandpass Filter Using Notch Structure Method for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: In this day and age, it is common for people to use electronic devices. Electronic devices that are becoming more sophisticated day by day require interconnection between other devices. To meet these needs, a filter can be used which can filter out certain desired frequencies. One type of filter used for wireless communications is the microstrip filter. One frequency that has a large bandwidth is ultra wideband (UWB). UWB is a network technology that can be used in wireless network applications with very high data transfer speeds which are classified as Short Range Wireless. In this research, the Notch Band method was used to change the UWB frequency to Multiband. This filter was simulated using ADS 2011 and CST 2016 software, manufactured using Duroid Rogers RT 5880 substrate with = 2.2, tan = 0.0009, and h = 1.575 mm, and measured using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA).

articleTitle: Identifying Influential Nodes in Hypergraph Using Isolating Centrality
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Understanding processes such as information dissemination and network resilience relies on pinpointing influential nodes within complex relationships. Conventional centrality measures, which are based on shortest path calculations, fall short in hypergraphs due to the complexity of paths involving multiple simultaneous relationships. Traditional metrics oversimplify the node influence and the stability of hyperedges. The Isolating Centrality measure is introduced in hypergraphs to address the drawback it specifically focuses on local structures. ISC assesses how the removal of a node affects the connectivity of hyperedges, providing a more detailed approach for identifying influential nodes. We assess the superiority performance of ISC over conventional centrality metrics and are evaluated through correlation analysis and the SIR model.

articleTitle: 5G New Radio Network Design at Frequency n38 in Ibu Kota Nusantara
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) is the new capital city of the Republic of Indonesia, which has been designated by the Government of the Republic of Indonesia in 2022. IKN will function as the administrative and governmental centre of the Republic of Indonesia. for this reason, the development of telecommunication networks in IKN needs to be improved. One of them is the 5G New Radio network which has a speed 20 times faster than the previous generation so that it can provide service needs in the field of communication. This research uses the n38 frequency because of its ability to accommodate optimal capacity and coverage. This 5G New Radio network design uses the n38 frequency with 40Mhz bandwidth which includes technical coverage and capacity. According to the research analysis, Technical Coverage IKN requires 186 gNodeB with an average SS-RSRP value of-59.98, an average SS-SINR of 27.17, and a Throughput of 295 Mbps. while Technical Capacity requires 43 gNodeB with an average SS-RSRP value of −69.92, an average SS-SINR of 30.27, and a Throughput of 306 Mbps.

articleTitle: Optimizing Delay Tolerant Networks with Multicopy Routing Protocols and Advanced Mobility Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of multicopy routing protocols in Delay-Tolerant Networks (DTNs) under realistic and dynamic conditions using two distinct mobility models: Shortest Path Map-Based Movement and Map-Based Movement. The analysis focuses on key performance metrics, including delivery probability, overhead ratio, average latency, and message drop rate across network configurations such as node counts, buffer sizes, and message copies (Lcopies). The results demonstrate that MaxProp consistently outperforms other protocols, including Prophet, Epidemic, and Spray-and-Wait, by achieving higher delivery probabilities, lower overhead ratios, reduced latency, and minimal message drop rates. A key contribution of this research lies in integrating realistic node mobility patterns and diverse buffer management strategies to optimize DTN performance. This study also highlights the practical implications of MaxProp's robustness in disaster response, rural connectivity, and environmental monitoring, where reliable data transmission is critical. These findings emphasize the importance of combining advanced routing strategies with efficient mobility-aware mechanisms to enhance scalability and reliability in DTN applications.

articleTitle: Indonesian Stock Price Prediction Using Random Effect Model with Technical Indicators in Panel Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: In the investment journey of a stock investor, the most critical factor influencing the growth of investor assets is stock selection. In investing, investors may lose money if they choose the wrong stocks. Stock Price Prediction Research on panel data based on Technical Indicators on the Stock Exchange of Indonesia aims to enhance stock price prediction results. Hence, everything runs smoothly in stock selection. This study develops a Random Effect Model (REM) statistical method combined with technical indicator data to enhance stock price prediction results and compare them with Predicted outcomes achieved by machine learning techniques. This study improves the prediction results for every model by including technical indicator data management in the prediction process. The results of this study indicate that the REM model is a superior model with an evaluation value of R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> 0.958, MAE 139.152, and MSE 218962.893. In the 2nd experiment, technical indicator data management successfully increased the Prediction results by R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> by 0.361, MAE by 308.172, and MSE by 1864456.653.

articleTitle: Smart Payment System for Supermarkets Based on Facial Recognition Technology and Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research develops a smart payment system for supermarkets, integrating item and facial recognition with customer emotion analysis, gender detection, and age estimation to optimize the shopping experience by exploiting the multi-task cascaded convolutional neural network (MTCNN), FaceNet, and VGG-Face models. On our creatively designed website platform, store owners can easily generate a unique QR code for each product with just a few simple steps. During the payment process, customers place the products on the counter, and immediately, the camera will capture the image so that our website can recognize the QR code, automatically generating a list of products along with their corresponding prices. An invoice will be generated, and the buyer can proceed with the payment as instructed. To complete the payment, customers must confirm their identity through facial recognition, helping the system accurately identify the buyer. Not stopping there, the system can also sense the user's emotions, thereby evaluating their shopping experience to some extent. The system improves operational efficiency, allows effective management, analyzes customer visit frequency, and provides personalized services. By incorporating AI technologies, the system brings significant benefits to improving supermarket operations.

articleTitle: Estimating Future Prices of Key Agricultural Commodities Using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Farmers, consumers, and policymakers face difficulties as a result of the price fluctuation of basic agricultural commodities like rice, tomatoes, onions, and dals. For better market stability and well-informed decision-making, accurate price forecasts are essential. In order to assess historical market data and forecast price patterns, this study proposes a machine learning-based method that makes use of regression and time-series forecasting models. The suggested models show superior accuracy than conventional statistical techniques by capturing the intricacies of price swings caused by seasonal demand and crop yields, promoting enhanced supply chain planning and efficiency in agriculture.

articleTitle: Late Fusion Approach for Facial Expression Recognition Using HOG, LBP, and DWT Features with SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is critical for applications in security, emotion analysis, and human-computer interactions. This work investigates the usage of a hybrid strategy that combines three feature extraction techniques Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) model. The objective is to improve the accuracy and resilience of FER systems by combining predictions from models trained on each feature set. The CK+48 dataset, which contains 22,410 photos across eight emotion classes, serves as the benchmark. The experimental findings reveal that separate feature extraction approaches (DWT, HOG, and LBP) achieve accuracies of 65.62%, 71.88%, and 47.19%, respectively. However, the late fusion model greatly increases performance, obtaining an overall accuracy of 93.44%. The late fusion approach combines the strengths of many characteristics to overcome issues including illumination fluctuations, face expressions, and occlusion. This work demonstrates the potential of late fusion to improve the reliability and accuracy of FER systems in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Analysis of Dual-Feed Dual-Polarized Microstrip Patch Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This study presents a detailed analysis of mutual coupling in two dual-polarized microstrip antenna elements, which plays a crucial role in optimizing performance for high-efficiency 5G communication systems. Each antenna element is designed with a dual coaxial feed to support two orthogonal polarizations, enabling both horizontal and vertical signal transmission and enhancing spectral efficiency. Mutual coupling is examined in horizontal and vertical orientations, with antenna elements spaced at half a wavelength at a frequency of 2.35 GHz. Experimental results indicate that the coupling between ports on the same antenna element (S21) achieves a low value of -31.9 dB, while coupling between separate elements (S31, S41, S32, S42) measures -24.7 dB, -50.1 dB, -47.6 dB, and -17.3 dB, respectively. The observed gain variation of 2.8 dBi, attributed to mutual coupling effects, provides valuable insights into the resulting signal efficiency and stability. These findings are crucial for optimizing dual-polarized antenna arrays, particularly in scenarios requiring compact, interference-resistant configurations, such as 5G base stations and dense MIMO systems. By effectively managing interference and maintaining consistent radiation patterns across different orientations, this design improves reliability, enhances spatial diversity, and minimizes cross-polarization interference. The study's outcomes underscore the dual-feed, dual-polarized antenna array's suitability for modern communication environments where low cost, high capacity, and compact size are essential. Future work will involve refining the antenna element spacing and exploring alternative feeding techniques to further reduce coupling and improve system resilience in more complex array applications.

articleTitle: Predict Mobile Legends Match Results Based on In-Game Conditions Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Mobile Legends, a popular Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) game, relies on team strategy and hero combinations to influence match results. Players and teams seek to enhance their performances by analyzing past matches, understanding opponents' tendencies, and planning appropriate strategies. However, many players face challenges in maintaining their rankings due to frequent losses. This study aims to predict match outcomes based on in-game conditions to help players make better strategic decisions. The research consists of five stages: data collection, data analysis, data preprocessing, data processing, and evaluation. Data is collected from random streamers, primarily those with Indonesian flags, including match duration, number of kills, and hero selections. The preprocessing stage involves selecting and converting attributes and set roles. A deep learning model using neural networks is applied to predict match results, evaluated by accuracy, precision, recall, and an F1-score metrics. The model achieved an accuracy of 89.62%, precision of 91.68%, recall of 93.13%, and F1-score of 92.34% with the rectifier activation function providing the best performance. These results indicate that deep learning can effectively enhance prediction models to facilitate better decision-making in games.

articleTitle: Two Distance Domination Numbers of Graphs Resulting from Amalgamation Operation of Combination of Path Graphs and Special Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The number of dominating nodes in a network that can control the surrounding linked nodes with the fewest amount of dominating nodes is known as the dominance number. In this research, the dominance number of distance two on the graph resulting from the amalgamation operation of the combination of path graphs and special graphs will be investigated. This is different from previous studies that have existed, namely both distance one and distance two domination numbers with ordinary amalgamation operations, without using a combination of path graphs and special graphs. This research emphasizes on the results of amalgamation operations of combinations of path graphs and special graphs. The method used in this research is pattern recognition and axiomatic deductive method. The results of this research are new theorems from the results of the amalgamation operation of the combination of path graphs and special graphs.

articleTitle: Soft Set Classification for Landslide Risk Level
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Landslides are common natural disasters and often cause significant damage to society. Predicting and controlling landslide disasters is essential because landslides threaten human production and life. When studying landslide risks and deciding whether to treat them, it is necessary to classify and compare them to select landslides with higher hazard levels. This study aims to generate a soft set of landslide risk classification (SSC). The five variables for SSC classification are slope, vegetation density, lithology, land use, and hydrological system. The results showed that the SSC reached 0.90 accuracy on training data and 0.950 for recall. Therefore, it is expected to be used to classify landslide risk levels.

articleTitle: Electromyograph-Based Finger Angle Estimation with Convolutional Neural Network Methods for Rehabilitation of Stroke Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Ischemic stroke often causes weakness in the fingers due to disruption or loss of signals between the brain and muscles, making rehabilitation essential for restoring motor function. In stroke rehabilitation technology, one method used is the exoskeleton robot, designed to assist movement in parts of the body affected by weakness. Developing an exoskeleton control system requires EMG signals to detect muscle activity and deep learning to predict hand muscle movements. This study proposes the use of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methods to develop hand movement predictions based on EMG signals. As technology advances, affordable and wearable EMG devices, such as the Myo Armband, have driven the development of regression-based hand exoskeleton control systems. The study results show that the CNN model achieved an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.68, with cross-validation R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> scores ranging from 0.72 to 0.84, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in improving motor rehabilitation and the predictive performance of finger movements.

articleTitle: On Optimal Network Topologies for Noise-Limited Wireless Mesh Networks with Delay Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Network densification is seen as one viable solution to provide the ample capacity for urban 5G networks. One of the technical challenges in this development is how to provide sufficient backhaul connectivity to all the new small cell base stations that will be installed to new types of locations like lamp posts and bus stops. One potential solution is to use multi-hop millimeter wave backhaul with beamforming antennas. In such wireless backhaul networks, interference is usually a minor issue and the connectivity is limited mostly by high attenuation. At the same time, one of the major challenges with multihop wireless networks is to meet the 5G delay budget. Furthermore, in this kind of deployment scenario, the fragility of millimeter wave links should be considered and thus the network resiliency increased by adopting partial mesh network topology. In this paper, we will show that in these type of networks and with given constraints the backhaul network topology should favor low node degree (3–4) over low hop-count. Furthermore, we will show that the spatial scaling constraints in realistic network deployments limit the network growth rate as the network diameter increases. This fact is then shown to reduce the scaling penalty of partial mesh topologies compared to tree structured networks. We will analyze the effects of spatial constraints by using an incremental network deployment simulation model. The results will indicate that, in practice, partial mesh network topology can achieve similar worst case delay targets compared to tree structured networks and that it is possible to compensate the small differences in scaling properties with minimal increases in BH node density.

articleTitle: Shadow Zone Analysis in Banda Sea Region Based on Profiling Float Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
