abstract: The Banda Sea is an essential part of the Indonesian Archipelago Sea Lane (ALKI) III, which is strategic but still minimally explored. The crucial position of the Banda Sea in international shipping lanes and maritime defense operations requires a more in-depth oceanographic study related to underwater defense strategies. In this study, the Arvor I profiling float operated by BMKG provides real-time data with Iridium satellite communication to observe oceanographic parameters such as temperature, salinity, and depth. This study aims to analyze the shadow zone, which has essential implications for underwater acoustic operations, especially submarine navigation. The research methodology includes analysis of vertical temperature and salinity profiles to identify the thermocline layer. The speed of sound is calculated using the McKenzie equation by considering variations in temperature, salinity, and sea depth. Acoustic propagation simulations were performed using the spherical spreading model approach to map the distribution of the shadow zone. The analysis results indicate the presence of a thermocline at a depth range of 44.7 to 1016.4 meters, with a minimum point of sound speed at a depth of around 992 meters. Understanding the distribution of this shadow zone can significantly contribute to the optimization of underwater acoustic operations in the Banda Sea region, including in supporting submarine operations and other acoustic monitoring activities.

articleTitle: Hybrid Approach for Procedural Level Generation for 2D Platformer Game
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research proposes a hybrid approach for a procedural level generation for our 2D platformer game. The method integrates manual level creation and procedural algorithm to generate a complete level for 2D rouge-like platformer game including the overall structure of the level, corridors, enemies, obstacles, and items. The proposed method also allowed user-input parameters that define requirement for the level such as difficulty, room numbers, enemy and item spawn probability. We developed the proposed method and implemented the system in our game, Lost Labyrinth Rouge's Odyssey. We implemented the system specifically to fit the mechanic and rules of our game. To test the performance of the system to develop a level, we performed a usability test by inviting users to play the game multiple times. The result and feedback from the respondents show that most the system was able to generate a good playability for a 2D platformer dungeon game.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Phase Detection Models for Indonesian On-site EEWS Using Strong Motion Accelerograph Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Indonesia is located in one of the most seismically active regions in the world, making early earthquake warning systems (EEWS) crucial for mitigating disaster impacts. This paper explores developing and implementing deep learning models for phase detection in Indonesia's on-site EEWS using a network of Strong Motion Accelerographs (SMA). Traditional seismic detection methods often face limitations in speed and accuracy when distinguishing between P-waves and S-waves, which are critical for early warnings. This study aims to assess phase detection models utilizing a deep learning method to predict P-Phase arrival times, harnessing Indonesian SMA data from 45,000 seismic occurrences. We used pre-trained from several published phase detection models and performed the models on data collected from Indonesian seismic networks, addressing challenges such as noisy data and varying geological conditions. The findings of this investigation reveal that the appropriate model for Indonesian EEWS is the GPD model, which exhibits a commendable equilibrium in performance. The results of this study indicate that the GPD model achieves an excellent time error value in determining the onset of the P-wave arrival with a very short data length of 2 seconds, yielding an error of 0.02 seconds, followed by PhaseNet with 0.05 seconds and EQTransformer with 0.09 seconds. Results demonstrate significant possibilities in detection speed and accuracy compared to conventional methods, making this approach a promising solution for enhancing the effectiveness of Indonesia's on-site EEWS. Our findings have important implications for disaster preparedness and response in earthquake-prone regions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Advanced Encryption Standard with Chaotic Map and Dynamic S-Box
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is one of cryptography algorithms widely used for protecting data across various sectors of technology. Although widely used, there are still some vulnerabilities in AES, notably the fixed S-Box and the lack of a MixColumn step in the final encryption round, which limit its resistance against specific cryptographic attacks. This paper proposes a new enhanced AES algorithm targeting 128 bit key encryption, including the introduction of dynamic S-Box to replace the fixed S-Box, key generation based on Chebyshev chaotic map, and modified encryption process incorporating MixColumn step in the final round and reduction of number of rounds. These modifications aims to increase complexity and improve resilient against decryption against unauthorized parties, while improving the performance of the algorithm. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed algorithm successfully enhanced both security and performance. The proposed algorithm achieves a higher average avalanche score of 53.02 %, surpassing the standard AES score of 50.00 %. For the encryption time, the proposed algorithm demonstrates faster encryption time across various file sizes, with a reduction of approximately 20% compared to the standard AES.

articleTitle: TDS Sensor Application in Laser Communication for Automatic Water Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: TDS automatic data collection was designed based on a sensor and Arduino board using red laser beam communication. The sensor was calibrated by measuring 4 different water solutions using a commercial TDS Meter compared with the TDS sensor output. The calibrated sensor was then tested in laser communication where the data processed by first Arduino was modulated by red laser frequency through pulse-width-modulation (PWM) schemes. The modulated signal was sent via a laser beam where solar cell captured it as a photodetector in the receiver. The received data was demodulated inside the second Arduino to be displayed in a serial monitor for communication performance observation. As the result, the link distance of TDS data transmission can reach 25 m and 4 m in free-space and water medium, respectively. When the transmission channel was a water environment, the link distance will be depended on PWM types utilized in the experiment.

articleTitle: Planning Based on Coverage and Capacity of 5G New Radio Using Frequency 2.3 GHz to Support Pegunungan Bintang Regency
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research aims to design a cellular network in Pegunungan Bintang Regency to support the development of 3T (Frontier, Outermost, Disadvantaged) areas in Indonesia. Simulations using Atoll software analyzed key parameters such as RSRP, SINR, and throughput. Results indicate that deploying 220 sites achieves 88.6% area coverage with reliable signal quality and an average throughput of 231336.67 Kbps, enabling high-bandwidth applications. In comparison, deploying 24 sites covers only 14.8% of the area with an average throughput of 225204.07 Kbps, sufficient for basic communication. Although the 220-site configuration requires higher investment, it offers transformative benefits, including extensive coverage, robust connectivity, and IoT support in vital sectors such as mining and plantations. This optimized gNodeB deployment not only overcomes geographical barriers but also catalyzes economic growth, presenting a sustainable solution for advancing regional development in 3T areas.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Tuning of U-Net for Active Fire Segmentation in Peatlands of Indonesia Using Landsat 8 Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This study focuses on fire segmentation in peatland areas using the U-Net model, involving hyperparameter tuning combined with data masking developed using a modified ToPeCAl algorithm. The data masking process utilizes TIRS-1 band, band 7, and band 6, while the training data consists of composite images from bands 7, 6, and 4 (764) and 7, 6, and 2 (762) for comparison. Input data includes image patches sized 128×128, 256×256, and 512×512, derived from the 764 and 762 composites, respectively. The study reveals that the use of the leakyReL U activation function, a dilation rate strategy, a learning rate schedule, 50% image patch overlap, and a patch size of 128×128, improves the model's performance for fire segmentation compared to the baseline model. The final evaluation metrics demonstrate Precision, Recall, F1 Score, and IoU values of 88.85%, 89.70%, 89.08%, and 77.36%, respectively.

articleTitle: The Effect of Laplace Smoothing on Naive Bayes for Sentiment Analysis of the Impact of the AstraZeneca Vaccine
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)

authors.preferredName: M. Fadhil Al Hikam Tirta Bayu Aj

abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has presented complex and disturbing challenges worldwide, affecting not only the health sector but also the global economy. One of the main strategies to respond to this pandemic is through mass vaccination, where the AstraZeneca vaccine has received emergency use authorization in many countries, including Indonesia. Although effective in reducing the risk of COVID-19 infection, the use of this vaccine has also raised concerns regarding rare side effects such as thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS). This study aims to determine the performance of the Naive Bayes model applying Laplace Smoothing in classifying public sentiment towards the side effects of the AstraZeneca vaccine on social media X, by measuring accuracy, precision, and recall. Data from social media platform X was used to analyze Indonesian public sentiment towards the side effects of the AstraZeneca vaccine. The Naive Bayes method with the application of Laplace Smoothing was used to classify comments originating from the platform into positive and negative. Showing an accuracy rate of around 72.08%, precision of around 70.70%, and recall of around 72.08%. The results of this analysis provide a deeper understanding of how the public interprets the side effects of this vaccine, which can support more effective public health policy-making and communication strategies in dealing with this pandemic globally.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Word2Vec, FastText, and Glove Embeddings for Synonym Identification in Bugis Language
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research aims to analyze the performance of word vectors generated by three pre-trained word embedding models, namely Word2Vec, Fast'Text, and Glove, to detect synonyms at the word level in the Bugis language. The word vectors from each model were integrated with a Bugis language dataset containing 12,060 monolingual texts, and then trained using the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model. The results show that Word2Vec has the highest accuracy of 0.9412, followed by Glove with 0.9353 and FastText with 0.9262. Additional experiments with cosine similarity revealed that Glove performed best for predicting synonyms across all word occurrence frequency categories, while FastText and Word2Vec had inferior results. These findings indicate that although high training accuracy is achieved, it does not always imply that the model will excel in predicting synonyms.

articleTitle: The Influence of Artificial Intelligence on Recommendation Features in E-commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research aims to investigate the key element that could influence purchase decision within the rapidly growing Indonesian e-commerce market, focusing on how the artificial intelligence (AI) powered recommendation system increases the purchasing intention by analyzing the user profile, behavior, search history, and preferences. In this study, 429 people were surveyed to find out how attitudes toward artificial intelligence are influenced by perceived utility, perceived ease of use, perceived risk, and how these factors, in conjunction with promotion display and hedonistic value (the enjoyment derived from shopping), influence purchase intention in Indonesia's e-commerce landscape. The findings' data support all of the proposed hypotheses. Perceive utility and ease of use with technology attitude are strong predictors in determining positive attitude towards Artificial Intelligence, while the perceived risk has a negative impact on this attitude. Moreover, the study also found that positive attitude towards Artificial Intelligence, alongside promotional display, and hedonistic value, plays a significant role in determining purchase intention of customers in Indonesia e-commerce. The study also shows that a positive response for those three components significantly enhances the overall purchase intention of the customers. This study provides a valuable insight for e-commerce platforms in Indonesia for increasing purchase intention and purchase conversion.)

articleTitle: Stock Price Index Prediction of Several ASEAN Countries Using Panel Data Regression and Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The analysis of major stock indices plays a crucial role in understanding market sentiment and predicting economic performance in the ASEAN region. Several studies have examined panel data regression and machine learning methods to analyze macroeconomic variables related to stock indices, including boosting models such as XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM, which have proven effective in handling the complexity of multivariable financial data. This study aims to explore the use of the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) to measure the impact of variables such as gold prices, dollar exchange rates, bond yields, and commodity prices on major stock indices, as well as employing machine learning for short-term forecasting. Daily data from 2019–2024 for ASEAN countries was used, with models selected based on significance tests, accuracy, MAE, MSE, and R2. The results show that LightGBM achieves the highest accuracy, with an MAE of 31.05 and 53.77, and an MSE of 3105.61 and 9786.65 on training and testing data, respectively, achieving 100% R2 on both. CatBoost and XGBoost also perform well, with high accuracy and low error values. Results show LightGBM as a reliable tool for projecting ASEAN stock market trends.

articleTitle: Dual Word Embedding Framework for Gender-Based Writing Style Analysis Using Word2Vec and BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Social media has evolved into a vast and multifaceted data repository, presenting valuable opportunities to investigate gender-based variations in writing styles. This study aims to enhance the precision of gender classification on Twitter text by leveraging a combined word embedding approach. The paper proposes a framework that utilizes two distinct word embedding models - a combination of GloVe and BERT, as well as GloVe and Word2Vec - to capture both global and contextual linguistic nuances within the text. The dataset comprises a comprehensive collection of tweets and user profile descriptions harvested from Twitter, which underwent meticulous preprocessing and word representation steps before being further processed using the robust Random Forest algorithm. The experimental findings indicate that the combination of GloVe and BERT outperforms the other combination of GloVe and Word2Vec, and also surpasses the performance of single embedding models, with 62.93% accuracy being the highest achieved result. This study provides valuable insights into the potential of combined word embedding techniques for enhancing the accuracy of gender classification in social media text analysis.

articleTitle: Designing an Application to Digitize Vietnamese Medical Records Using OCR Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: In today's developed society, hospitals in Vietnam have almost computerized paperwork in medical records. However, storing electronic medical records (EMR) and gradually replacing paper medical records is a breakthrough and only a few large hospitals and some private facilities have piloted it. EMR implementation in Vietnam is progressing very slowly compared to the prescribed implementation roadmap. Even when EMR is implemented, previously paper medical records must continue to be stored according to current regulations. Therefore, there is a need for an effective solution to digitize these existing paper medical records so that they can be used and stored most effectively. Some recent solutions enhance the application of optical character recognition (OCR) technology to build medical record management software for departments, optimally supporting medical record storage. Patient records are preserved carefully and better, looking up information and medical records quickly and accurately, avoiding wasting a lot of time searching. This article focuses on extracting information from Vietnamese paper medical records using Tesseract and Google OCR tools. In addition to image processing techniques, the research also builds diagrams of optimal user interaction algorithms on the web application platform. The system uses mobile cameras to take pictures, transmit them to the processing server, then extract the necessary information, and finally automatically enter the information into the hospital database. By exploiting image and text processing techniques, the system's performance achieved a recognition success rate of 83% without interaction and improved significantly to over 90% with basically manual editing image input from web users. Furthermore, it also can display extraction results for users to edit before saving them to the database.

articleTitle: SDGCN: Span Dual-Channel Graph Convolutional Networks for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction (ASTE) iden-tifies terms of aspect, terms of opinion, and sentiments in text. Early approaches to the ASTE task, used token-level models, were prone to errors during decoding, affecting accuracy. Span-level models address this by capturing interactions between aspect and opinion spans. But encounters challenges due to sentence encoding methods that primarily rely on contextual data without utilizing syntactic and semantic information. This limitation lead to an inaccurate interpretation of complex sentiment interactions. This study proposes a span-based model that combines syntactic encoding through dependency parsing and graph convolutional networks, along with semantic encoding using multi-head attention and graph convolutional networks. Experimental results on four public datasets show the model achieves a precision of 74.9%, recall of 67.12%, and F1 score of 71.7%, providing an average improvement of 3% over span-based methods in aspect sentiment triplet extraction.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Graph NLP Assistant for Mitigate Norm Violations: Live Chat Moderation Study
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The rise of real-time communication through live chat and social media platforms has heightened the need for effective content moderation tools to detect and mitigate norm violations, such as hate speech, abusive language, and offensive slang, thereby ensuring user safety. This study develops and evaluates a knowledge-graph-based natural language processing (NLP) framework aimed at improving the accuracy and efficiency of content moderation in live chats. Several machine learning models were explored, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Neural Network (NN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), along with their graphenhanced variants. The models were trained and evaluated on a comprehensive dataset including various norm violations. Results show that the Graph-Bi-LSTM model outperforms the others, achieving an F1-score of 0.84, precision of 0.84, and accuracy of 0.81, indicating its potential to improve harmful content detection. Despite these promising outcomes, the study underscores the need for human oversight to prevent false positives and ensure context-aware decision-making. The findings suggest that combining graph-based NLP models with human moderation tools can enhance the transparency and reliability of content moderation in real-time. Further research should optimize the inference time of models and continuously adapt the system to handle evolving language trends and diverse cultural contexts.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Insights into High School Market Segmentation Using Multidimensional Clustering Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: In the increasingly competitive landscape of higher education, market segmentation has become essential for institutions to effectively target prospective students. High school segmentation allows universities to tailor their recruitment strategies based on diverse factors. This study presents a multidimensional approach to segmenting high schools using K-Means Clustering and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The goal is to identify distinct clusters based on key attributes such as academic quality, student quantity, financial background, and geographical proximity, providing insights for higher education institutions (HE Is) to optimize recruitment strategies. The dataset, comprising 363 high schools after data preprocessing, was analyzed using clustering techniques. The results reveal five distinct clusters, with marketing priorities focusing on Clusters 1, 2, 3, and 4, which represent 68% of the target market. This research offers actionable insights for HEIs to refine resource allocation and enhance their outreach efforts to effectively engage prospective students.

articleTitle: Optimizing Feature Selection for Stock Price Prediction Using a Two-Stage Feature Selection Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Stock price prediction with stock price history and technical indicators has challenges in high feature dimensions. Recursive feature elimination feature selection is one solution to overcome this. However, there are several disadvantages to recursive feature elimination. Depending on the machine learning model used, the highest feature ranking may not always be the most relevant, and it also requires lengthy computation time. This study proposes feature selection optimization for stock price prediction using a two-stage feature selection framework. Stage 1 feature selection uses a combination of minimum and maximum that are relevant to the concept of quotient and important random forest features. Stage 2 feature selection uses recursive feature elimination. The stock data used are PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), and PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk (BBTN). The prediction results show that the RMSE in the proposed method gets the best value under 20 features, and the MAPE value in the proposed method gets a value that is always smaller than other methods. This proves that the Two-Stage Feature Selection Framework successfully optimizes feature selection for stock price prediction, thereby reducing the error rate of stock price prediction.

articleTitle: Leveraging the Pre-Trained Whisper Model and Levenshtein Distance for Audio Buginesse Transcription
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research aims to transcribe audio into text using the pre-trained Whisper model, focusing on Bugis, a low-resource language. A key challenge in transcribing local languages like Bugis is the limited availability of language model. To address this, we implemented an algorithmic correction approach that does not require extensive datasets or computationally demanding customizations. The Whisper model provides an initial transcription, serving as a foundation; however, the output often lacks accuracy due to the absence of specific adjustments for Bugis. To enhance accuracy, we applied the Levenshtein distance algorithm to correct word errors by comparing transcription results with entries in a Bugis language dataset based on similarity. Although this method is not fully precise and depends on the completeness of the reference dataset, evaluation results indicate that it effectively lowers the word error rate (WER) and improves transcription accuracy. This research produces SRT files containing transcripts that have been corrected using the Levenhstein distance algorithm, which not only improves accessibility but also contributes to the preservation of Bugis language through digital media. This approach is expected to provide a practical solution to improve transcription accuracy and support more accurate documentation in Bugis language preservation efforts.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network (DNN) for Outlier Detection in Heavy Metal Voltammetric Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The majority of existing outlier detection methods are unable to adequately address the inherent complexity and variability of voltammetry data, particularly in the context of heavy metal detection. The effectiveness, precision, and adaptability of these methods are constrained, particularly when confronted with complex datasets. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel outlier detection method combining Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, Local Outlier Factor (LOF), Z-Score, and Deep Neural Network (DNN) techniques. The proposed approach is designed to enhance accuracy by leveraging the unique strengths of each method in identifying outliers within complex data. Evaluation results demonstrate that the DNN method achieves the highest accuracy, reaching 99.87%, significantly outperforming other tested models. This robust performance suggests that the proposed method has substantial potential to improve the reliability of detecting heavy metal anomalies in voltammetric data. Specifically, the DNN method demonstrated an F1-score of 1.00 across multiple evaluation metrics, outperforming other models such as Isolation Forest (F1-score: 0.65) and LOF (F1-score: 0.75).

articleTitle: Exploratory Data Analysis to Improve the Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks in Online Sales Product Image Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Online sales item prediction has become essential for effective business planning. Digital transformation has enabled companies to collect much data on consumer behavior, market trends, and other factors influencing sales performance. This research's problem is identifying relevant patterns and predicting sales growth based on uploaded images and image names. Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) have been widely used in analyzing sequential data, such as online sales data, due to their ability to capture temporal dependency patterns. However, the performance of CNNs is highly dependent on the quality and prior understanding of the data used. Therefore, this study proposes to improve the performance of CNNs in online sales prediction. In this study, Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is an important step in improving the performance of CNNs in online sales prediction. EDA helps identify trends, seasonality, and autocorrelation patterns in sales data and detects missing values, outliers, and other variations that require special handling. The results show that EDA improves the performance, stability, and interpretability of the CNN model, and helps reduce bias and variance in prediction, as evidenced by the results of loss: 0.0702 mae: 0.1929 for epoch: 10, loss: 0.0724 mae: 0.1913 for epoch: 15, loss: 0.0720 mae: 0.1894 for epoch: 20. The higher the epoch value, the smaller the loss and mae results. EDA improves comprehensive performance, and CNN can predict sales more accurately, improve efficiency, and reduce overfitting in the model.

articleTitle: An Exploration of Virtual Environments as Therapeutic Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Given the scale of the mental health situation globally and the fact that medical service providers struggle to accommodate the large number of patients, technologies such as Virtual Reality are being widely explored as mediums to deliver sustainable mental health services. However, even though the concept of VR as a tool for exposure therapy has been tested in different case studies, the area requires new information and directions on designing and testing such interventions, primarily due to the subjective nature of engineering solutions and setting expectations for a wide set of user stakeholders. This paper examines a pair of case studies in stress and phobias and offers some insight into how successful prototypes can appear and what user traits affect the overall results. Results indicate that effectiveness is correlated to parameters such as levels of immersion, attitude towards technology, age, and that such parameters are candidates for predictors of the confidence that participants gain. Preliminary tests of the developed prototyped show that there is a temporal decrease in the self-reported experienced discomfort throughout the interventions. The results reinforce the demand for VR intervention design guidelines and customization procedures before deployment.

articleTitle: Grammar Error Correction in Indonesian Sports News: Comparing the Performance of Pre-Trained T5 and BART Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research compares the performance of two pre-trained models based on the transformer, namely text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) and bidirectional and auto-regressive transformer (BART), through a fine-tuned for correcting grammar in Indonesian sports news texts. We used vennify/t5-base-grammar-correction and onionLad/grammar-correction-bart-base, was trained using a dataset of 10,075 sentences from Indonesian language sports news sites. We tested the model performance using bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU), google's language evaluation understanding (GLEU), training loss, and validation loss. The results show that BART was more efficient in learning data patterns and has better generalization ability, supported by BLEU and GLEU scores of 0.8560 and 0.9655. Meanwhile, T5 maintains simpler sentence structures, supported by BLEU and GLEU scores of 0.8120 and 0.9564. BART excels at handling more complex contexts, making it more effective at accurately correcting errors in dynamic sports news. Both models have their respective advantages, with BART being better at correcting detailed grammatical errors, while T5 offers consistent correction of more simple sentence structures.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Simulation for Estimating Production and Revenue Losses in Airport Services Due to Unplanned Power Outages: Insights for Mitigation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Unplanned power outages at airports can have operational impacts, such as disruption of communication systems and flight safety, disruption of airport information systems and security systems, passenger delays, flight delays and cancellations, and disruption of passenger service facilities. These impacts affect the production volume and revenue stream generated by the airport. This study aims to estimate and mitigate production and revenue losses on aeronautical and non-aeronautical services caused by unplanned power outages at airports in Indonesia. Data were collected from company reports, which included two major power outages, with durations of 5 hours 11 minutes and 1 hour 13 minutes. Monte Carlo simulations to estimate outage durations from 1 to 6.4 hours were conducted for 10,000 iterations and used normal distribution patterns. The results of this study show that the estimated average lost production for aeronautical services and non-aeronautical services ranged from 18982 to 121485 units and 19341 to 123082 units, respectively. Meanwhile, the average estimated lost revenue for aeronautical services and non-aeronautical services ranged from 720 to 4606 million rupiah and 400 to 2560 million rupiah, respectively. This study has limitations, such as the company's annual data that cannot capture actual variations in peak and off-peak hours and normal distribution patterns that may not represent extreme outage scenarios. The findings from this study provide insights to inform mitigation strategies that can be used to improve operational resilience and ensure service quality during power outages.

articleTitle: Real Time Detection of Coffee Bean Defects Using YOLO Method and SAHI (Slicing Aided Hyper Inference) Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The traditional coffee bean quality assessment process is time-consuming and subjective, relying heavily on the expertise of a Q grader. Therefore, accurate and real-time technology is required for detecting coffee bean defects. This research employs the YOLOv8 method with the addition of the SAHI (Slicing Aided Hyper Inference) framework to detect full black and partial black defects in Robusta coffee beans. The dataset consists of 300 grams of Robusta coffee beans sourced from Sumberwadung Coffee Plantation in Jember, East Java. A deep learning approach was used, incorporating the YOLOv8 model and SAHI techniques to enhance the detection accuracy of small objects. The developed model is capable of real-time inference, making it suitable for practical applications in the coffee industry. The study utilized two data-splitting scenarios: 70:20:10 and 80:10:10. Evaluation results indicated high Precision (P), Recall (R), and Mean Average Precision (mAP), with mAP values exceeding 0.99 across all scenarios. In the 70:20:10 split, the model achieved a Precision of 0.984, Recall of 0.97, and mAP of 0.994 for all classes. In the 80:10:10 split, the model recorded a Precision of 0.969, Recall of 0.983, and mAP of 0.993.

articleTitle: Balancing Noise Reduction and Signal Preservation in EEG Signal for Mental Stress Detection Through Comparative Analysis of Filtering Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This study conducts a comparative analysis of Kalman, Savitzky-Golay, Median, and Fixed Lag filters in enhancing EEG signal quality for mental stress detection. EEG data were collected from 40 participants (26 males, 14 females) using a 32-channel Emotiv Epoc Flex headset, sampled at 128 Hz. The participants engaged in stress-inducing arithmetic problems, Stroop tests, and mirror image identification. These tasks were designed to create varying levels of mental stress, which were essential for analyzing the effectiveness of filtering techniques in noise reduction and signal preservation. The effectiveness of each filter was assessed based on performance metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and the reduction in Standard Deviation (STD) and Variance (VAR). The Kalman Smoother gave a moderate performance: an MSE of 1122.07, MAE of 21.43, RMSE of 31.94, and noise reduction of 13.4% in STD and 62.72% in VAR. Also, the Savitzky-Golay filter performed moderately, which slightly underperformed in comparison with the Kalman filter. The Median filter shows high accuracy of the signal with low values of MSE, MAE, and RMSE; notwithstanding, it has low noise reduction, as can be viewed by low STD and VAR reduction. The Fixed Lag filter is very good in noise reduction, reducing STD and VAR significantly, while incurring higher errors with increased MSE, MAE, and RMSE. These findings suggest that the Kalman filter is effective for noise reduction, excessive smoothing may remove essential signal information, potentially impacting detection accuracy. Future research could explore adaptive filtering that dynamically balance noise reduction and signal preservation, thereby enhancing EEG-based mental health assessments.

articleTitle: A Study on SME Traditional Food Product Feedback by Leveraging Word2vec
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The impact of reviews on sellers can be seen in improving services, products and communication. Small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) sadly lack the ability to properly manage review data on social media channels, which might provide insightful analysis of the things they sell. This study focuses on examining the review associated with traditional food in e-commerce and find the accuracy of Skip-Gram and Continous Bag of Words (CBOW). The review will use word2vec as a word embedding. Word2vec will predicts words based on Skip-Gram and CBOW. For modeling data the experiment use random forest and support vector machine and evaluated by confusion matrix. The result presents that Continuous Bag of Words surpasses the accuracy of skip-gram in two conditions splitting data which is 83,5% for 9 training: 1 testing and 85,5 for 7 training: 3 testing.

articleTitle: Analyzing Student Ethical Perception on ChatGPT Usage in Indonesian Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This study explores the ethical implications and factors influencing ChatGPT adoption in Indonesian higher education. Indonesia presently leads Southeast Asia in ChatGPT usage due to younger generations who are quick to adopt new technology into their daily life. ChatGPT's growing role in education has resulted in numerous benefits, such as intelligent tutoring systems, personalized help, and adaptable learning experiences that have reshaped the learning process. However, students may become overly dependent on this tool, which could undermine the goal of education by weakening higher-level cognitive abilities like creativity, problem-solving, and critical thinking. This research, therefore, set out to evaluate students' knowledge, attitudes, perspectives, concerns, and ethical considerations around ChatGPT usage. Using a quantitative approach, data were collected via an online questionnaire from 512 student respondents and analysed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results showed that four of the five proposed hypotheses were supported and revealed that knowledge of ChatGPT has no significant impact on its usage, whereas students' attitudes did play a critical role. Moreover, ChatGPT usage significantly influenced students' views, concerns, and their perceptions of ethical considerations. This study provides a novel, student-centered perspective on the ethical considerations of AI in education and sparks discussion on establishing appropriate, accountable use of ChatGPT in Indonesia's higher education system.

articleTitle: Leveraging Graph-Based for Enhanced Service Identification and Microservices Partitioning in Business Process Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Business process systems face critical challenges in identifying and partitioning microservices, particularly in Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems where complex interdependencies and dynamic workflows make it difficult to establish optimal service boundaries. Traditional service identification approaches often rely on manual analysis or basic clustering techniques, lacking the capability to effectively capture and analyze intricate service relationships and dependencies. Furthermore, existing methods struggle to provide quantifiable metrics for assessing service quality and optimizing service boundaries in complex business processes. To address these limitations, this research introduces a novel graph-based approach utilizing Neo4j for enhanced service identification and microservices partitioning. The approach incorporates three key innovations: (1) automated extraction of service dependencies from Business Process Model and Notation diagrams to reduce manual effort and potential errors, (2) comprehensive structural analysis through graph database capabilities for deeper understanding of service relationships, and (3) advanced quality metrics evaluation framework combining multiple dimensions including cohesion, coupling, granularity, and maintainability. Experimental evaluation across multiple ERP modules demonstrates the effectiveness of the approach, showing significant improvements in service autonomy (up to 94 percent), maintainability (80–85 percent enhancement), and modularity (up to 100 percent improvement). While achieving optimal service boundaries and improved system comprehension, the approach reveals an important trade-off between system maintainability and service cohesion that provides valuable insights for future research directions in microservices architecture optimization.

articleTitle: Handling Missing Value and Outlier to Improve Model Performance for Predicting Logistic Case
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The world of logistics is a world that urgently needs speed and accuracy in operational calculations. In order to support these operational needs, the logistics industry needs to keep up with the times by utilizing machine learning in its business processes. However, problems when utilizing machine learning in the industrial world include incomplete data and abnormal or outlier data caused by certain factors. This researcher will focus on improving machine learning models using KNN-Imputer to overcome incomplete data or missing values and Local Factor Outlier to overcome abnormal data. The results of the study show that when the extraction feature is utilized, the accuracy level of machine learning increases by 34.86% and decreases error by MAE 97.47%, MSE 99.72%, and RMSE 96.75%.

articleTitle: Ising Neo-Normal Model (INNM) for Segmentation of Cardiac Ultrasound Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Ultrasound imaging is challenging due to more noise. This paper proposed a segmentation model that improves model-based clustering that can be used for reduced noise in ultrasound imaging. The main contribution is combining spatial statistical mechanic effects (the Ising model) with non-symmetrical data distribution (Neo-Normal), which is called the Ising Neo-Normal Model (INNM). The model was achieved due to the limitation of GMM (Gaussian Mixture Model), which used symmetrical distributional and ignored the neighbors of pixels. Model estimation used the Bayesian method with the MCMC framework that combines Variational Inference with Gibbs Sampling. The performance of INNM was evaluated using the G-Mean and Jaccard Index with GMM and Bayesian Gaussian Mixture, and it was over 70%. INNM also gives better results than GMM and Bayesian Gaussian Mixture in cardiac ultrasound image data and simulation image data with various kinds of noise.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Utilizing Gabor, LBP, and HOG Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of vision loss, highlighting the need for timely diagnostic tools. This study explores machine learning techniques for DR classification using K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest classifiers. Retinal image features were extracted through Gabor filters, Local Binary Pattern (LBP), and Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG). The dataset, sourced from Kaggle, contains thousands of retinal images labeled by DR severity and collected under diverse imaging conditions. Images were split into training, validation, and testing subsets in an 8:1:1 ratio. The experimental workflow included preprocessing, feature extraction, model training, and evaluation based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Random Forest combined with HOG features achieved the highest accuracy of 73.02% and an F1-score of 61.63%. Despite this, the relatively low F1 score highlights the need for improvement in recall and precision. Limitations include reliance on traditional feature extraction and the exclusion of advanced deep-learning techniques. Future work should focus on integrating hybrid models that combine traditional feature extraction with deep learning, alongside using larger and more diverse datasets, to enhance diagnostic performance. These findings underline the potential for improving DR classification reliability

articleTitle: IoT-Based Recommendation System for Citrus Land Suitability Using Mamdani Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has enabled innovative applications in agriculture, addressing critical challenges faced by farmers. This study proposes designing and implementing an IoT-based recommendation system for citrus land suitability using the Mamdani fuzzy logic. The system integrates real-time data collection from environmental sensors, cloud-based storage, and fuzzy logic processing to generate actionable farmer recommendations. Key parameters such as temperature, soil moisture, and light intensity are collected using IoT sensors and processed to categorize land suitability into “Highly Suitable,” “Moderately Suitable,” and “Not Suitable” levels. Field tests with over 2,500 data points demonstrated a 92% match rate with expert evaluations, validating the system's accuracy and reliability. Farmers positively received the system's usability, highlighting its potential to enhance decision-making and optimize citrus cultivation.

articleTitle: Building of a Question-Answering System for Umrah Using Fine-Tuned Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This research examines the application of fine-tuning on Transformer models to develop a question-answering (QA) system. We designed this model to answer questions about Umrah accurately. Access to complete and relevant information about Umrah often poses a challenge for prospective pilgrims, especially when faced with specific questions that require a deep understanding of the religious context. We used the facebook/blenderbot-400M-distill model as a base retrained with a dataset containing 15,000 question-answer pairs related to Umrah. The model's fine-tuning process includes data tokenization, embedding, analysis of token length distribution, and hyperparameter optimization. We evaluate the model's performance using the perplexity metric to assess the accuracy and relevance of the model's responses. The results show that after training, the model achieved a perplexity value of 1.9494, with a training loss of 0.5087 and a validation loss of 0.6704, indicating good predictive capability.

articleTitle: Comparing Rayleigh Waves for Seismograph Health Diagnostics Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The need for high-quality seismic data requires the development of seismograph health diagnostic methods to detect instrument problems early. The rapid expansion of seismic networks, increasing data volume, and the growing complexity of analysis methods for detecting component degradation are challenged by limited resources. To overcome this problem, a more efficient method is needed to assess the health of seismographs at each station. We propose a simple seismograph health diagnostic method that uses machine learning to classify seismographs based on their condition. This method analyzes parameters derived from the similarity of teleseismic Rayleigh waves recorded by a target station and several nearby reference stations. Key metrics, including cross-correlation coefficient, amplitude ratio, and cross-spectral density coherence (CSD), are essential to label the condition of each station based on its actual status when the teleseismic event occurs, thus creating a comprehensive dataset. We rigorously evaluated this dataset using three leading classification models: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Among these, XGBoost demonstrated superior performance, achieving the highest accuracy (0.97), precision (0.99), recall (0.97), and F1 score (0.98). These results establish XGBoost as a reliable method for assessing seismograph health, classifying their status as excellent, good, fair, or poor. This approach is expected to enhance the seismograph health diagnostic and improve seismic network reliability.

articleTitle: Harmonizing Sentiments: User Reviews from Social Media of Kuta Beach as a Tourist Attraction
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Google Maps as a type Social Media is a popular navigation application created by Google. Since the market was very big and there are around 17.000 islands spread across the country, Indonesians use this application alot. Almost every tourist destination and place is here. Bali was one of the most visited places of Indonesia, reaching an outstanding 6,311,292 people and 36.91% of them were tourists. At Bali, Kuta Beach was one of the most visited and one of the most popular places in Bali. At the time of writing this research, the total number of reviews at Kuta Beach from Google Maps reached 39.638 reviews in total and rated 4.5 stars overall. This sentiment analysis research will be conducted by applying various classification models, such as Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. The research will begin with a data collection process, where web scraping will be implemented to extract the sample data. The data will then undergo a Data and Text process, involving labeling, case folding, and various data cleaning methods, including normalization, removal of stopwords, tokenization, and stemming. The processed sample data will be divided in an 80:20 ratio, with 80% of the data used for training and 20% for testing. Following this, the data will be applied to the classification models. The results of the various classification models will be compared to identify which one among the three has the highest accuracy. Through this research, it was found that Random Forest has the highest accuracy rate, reaching 89%.

articleTitle: Comparison of Clustering Algorithms with Categorical Data in Profiling Student Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Recognizing student characteristics in the context of modern education is a challenge in building an effective learning process. This research aims to identify diverse student profiles by applying clustering techniques on the categorical dataset of Advancing Education in Muslim Societies, which consists of 4,399 rows of data and 54 features. This dataset has undergone preprocessing stages using the PCA and Similarity-Based concepts, modelling using clustering algorithms, and evaluations that begin with feature selection related to self-regulation and selecting student data as the main dataset. This research successfully identified two different groups of students using the K-Means, Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering (AHC), and DBSCAN algorithms. Evaluation using the silhouette score shows that the Similarity-Based K-Means algorithm with a value of 0.9498 with a time of 0.2766 produces the most optimal clustering compared to the AHC and DBSCAN algorithms. The clustering results revealed two main clusters: the first cluster falls within the moderate SRL category, where students tend to exhibit reflective behaviors, such as appreciating experiences and learning from mistakes. However, they lack consistency in setting and evaluating the achievement of personal goals. In contrast, the second cluster represents high SRL, where students demonstrate strong self-regulation abilities with a high commitment to achieving their goals. They also exhibit a strong enthusiasm for learning and enjoy collaborating with others.

articleTitle: Comparison of Multilayer Perceptron Models for Spine X-Ray Image Classification Based on Hu Moment Invariant Features
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Spinal health is a critical factor significantly influencing human quality of life. However, diagnosing spinal conditions remains challenging due to the time-consuming process and the susceptibility to inaccuracies caused by noise and artifacts in medical images. To address these limitations, this study proposed an automated spine classification system designed to enhance accuracy and efficiency. A comparative analysis of three Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) training models-Bayesian Regularization (MLP-BR), LevenbergMarquardt (MLP-LM), and Scaled Conjugate Gradient (MLP-SCG)-was conducted using Hu Moment invariant features extracted from spinal images. The experimental results demonstrated that the MLP-BR model consistently outperformed other models across all hidden node configurations, achieving the highest average training accuracy of 99.7% and testing accuracy of 92.5% at a hidden node configuration of 15. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the MLP-BR model in spine image classification, providing a reliable and efficient solution to support accurate spinal health diagnoses.

articleTitle: Social Network Analysis (SNA) on Predicting Shipment Frauds in Consignment Goods
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The issue of fraud in consignment goods is a growing concern in the import sector. With an annual volume exceeding 61 million items, limited manpower among customs officers, smuggling of prohibited items and tax evasion there is an urgent need for effective tools to detect fraud. However, the highly imbalanced and feature-limited nature of consignment goods datasets makes accurate fraud classification challenging. This study explores techniques to leverage the dataset's unique characteristics, employing Social Network Analysis (SNA) to uncover intricate connections within consignment goods data. Five models with inherent strategies for handling imbalanced data were evaluated for fraud classification. The models were tested on three feature sets, with the final one combining SNA with personal features. Among the models, XGBoost achieved score of 1.000 on F1, Accuracy, Precision, Recall and AUC-PR Score. SNA proved effective in enhancing fraud classification on consignment goods datasets.

articleTitle: Lead (Pb) Contaminant Measurement on Distilled Water Using Hybrid Sensors and Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Heavy metals such as Pb, Hg, Cd, and As are commonly found in rivers and drinking water and can cause various health problems. This research aims to develop a linear regression model to predict the concentration of heavy metals (Pb) in distilled water based on TDS and pH sensors. Six experimental scenarios were utilized, each with different training data but the same testing data. A total of 30 rows of data were collected, each comprising five sets of data with Pb concentrations of 10 ppm, 20 ppm, 30 ppm, 40 ppm, 50 ppm, and 60 ppm. One data point from each concentration was randomly selected as test data. The rest are used to six form training data: raw, average, median, maximum, minimum, and skewness. The model's performance was evaluated using R2 and RMSE. The analysis results indicated that the raw training data model achieved the best performance, with the highest R2 value and the lowest RMSE. Further analysis showed that AVG_TDS had the most significant impact on predicting Pb concentrations.

articleTitle: Push-Up Movement Detection and Counting System Using MPU6050 Accelerometer Sensor Based on Arduino
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: This study presents a real-time push-up movement detection and quality evaluation system using the MPU6050 accelerometer sensor on the Arduino platform. The system integrates advanced algorithms, including Kalman filtering, to enhance sensor accuracy and reduce noise in body position tracking. Comparative analysis shows that the Kalman filter effectively smooths raw sensor data, ensuring precise detection of upward and downward phases during push-ups. From device testing, discrepancies between manual and device observations were recorded, with an average discrepancy of 3 points for the first respondent, and 1–2 points for the others. These discrepancies were due to rapid movements when respondents reached their maximum push-up points, affecting the device's responsiveness. Despite these differences, the system demonstrated an overall accuracy of 81.5%, validating its effectiveness. The approach improves push-up detection and repetition counting, making it suitable for real-time fitness applications for cadet at the Indonesian Air Force Academy.

articleTitle: Decision Support System for Internet Service Selection Using the Logarithmic Least Squares Weighting and Weighted Product Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Choosing the right internet service is an important challenge in today's digital era, especially for users who need reliability and optimal performance according to specific needs. This article proposes a decision support system (DSS) for internet service selection using a combination of Logarithmic Least Squares Weighting (LLSW) and Weighted Product Method (WPM) methods. The LLSW method is used to objectively determine the weight of the criteria based on the available data, while the WPM is used to evaluate and rank the available internet service alternatives. The purpose of the study is to implement a decision support system that can help users in choosing the best internet service by considering various important criteria objectively by combining LLSW and WPM methods to create an effective evaluation model for internet service selection. The study considers a variety of important criteria, such as data transfer speed, subscription fees, connection stability, number of devices, and customer service. The recommendation results showed that Biznet Home, First Media, and Indihome received the highest scores, indicating that these two services may be the top choice for users based on the assessment criteria used. The test results show that this decision support system is able to provide accurate and reliable recommendations in choosing the internet service that best suits the needs of users. This system is expected to help consumers in making more informed and effective decisions.

articleTitle: Gender-Based Bimodal Analysis of Speech and Text in Non-Contextual Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Emotion recognition can help human-computer interactions by enabling systems to respond empathetically and adapt to users' emotional conditions. This capability improves user experience, supporting the development of a more intuitive and emotionally responsive communication system. This study analyzes a bimodal approach based on gender (male and female) to recognize emotions without contextual information in dialogue analysis. Utilizing the Multimodal EmoryNLP dataset extracted from the TV series Friends with acted speech, we focused on four primary emotions: Angry, Neutral, Joy, and Scared. The model used in this study for text classification is RoBERTa, and wav2vec 2.0 is used for audio feature extraction with the Bi-LSTM model for classification. The experiment results using weighted F1-score reveal that data augmentation enhanced the performance of analyzing the original dataset from 0.46% to 0.52% and the male dataset from 0.43% to 0.51 %. In comparison, the female dataset remained consistent at 0.46%. The weighted F1-score and Unweighted Averaged Recall (UAR) from the male dataset are higher, 51 % and 48%, respectively, than those from the female dataset, 46% and 47%, respectively. Gender-based analysis indicated that male and female datasets exhibited distinct performance patterns, highlighting variations in emotional expression and recognition between genders. These findings underscore the effectiveness of multimodal strategies in emotion recognition and suggest that gender-specific factors play a significant role in enhancing classification performance. While these results highlight performance trends, further validation through repeated trials and statistical analyses could provide stronger generalizations and insights into gender-based differences.

articleTitle: Blood Segmentation in Crossmatch Test Images Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)

authors.preferredName: Ida Bagus Kade Rainata Putra Wibawa

abstract: In blood transfusion services, crossmatch testing (pretransfusion) is essential to prevent patient complications. However, the main problem faced is the reading and documentation of the crossmatched test results which are still done manually. This can hamper hospital services if not supported by an adequate number of health workers. Therefore, this research aims to help hospital services so that recording medical records is no longer manual. It can allocate health workers more efficiently through the automation of reading and storing the results of the crossmatch test with the deep learning model of image segmentation that has been made. The methods used in the research include data collection, data preprocessing and augmentation, model training, and model evaluation. The model used in this research implements an encoder and decoder-type architecture. In the experiment, three types of encoder and decoder are implemented, such ResNet34, ResNeXt50, and EfficientNet for the encoder and Feature Pyramid Network (FPN), Pyramid Attention Network (PAN), and DeepLabV3+ for the decoder. The result shows that the best model used ResNeXt50 encoder and PAN decoder with IoU score, F1 score, precision, recall, and accuracy of 0.9371, 0.8636, 0.9152, 0.9238, 0.9811, respectively.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Text Normalization Techniques for Enhanced Sentiment Analysis Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Sentiment analysis on Indonesian social media, particularly on platforms like Twitter, faces challenges due to the prevalence of informal and non-standard language. This variation complicates natural language processing (NLP) tasks, necessitating robust language normalization techniques. This study evaluates five normalization methods Jaro, Jaro Winkler, Levenshtein, Damerau-Levenshtein, and Smith-Waterman by comparing their effectiveness in enhancing sentiment classification accuracy on Indonesian Twitter data. The methods are tested against a standard word set (KBBI) and sentiment-labeled review data from the DANA application. Results indicate that Damerau-Levenshtein achieves the highest accuracy of 89.15% in classifying sentiments into positive and negative categories. Meanwhile, the Jaro method demonstrates strong consistency in handling errors like duplication and character insertion, albeit with slightly lower accuracy. These findings highlight the critical role of language normalization in improving NLP performance and provide actionable insights for developers working on sentiment analysis systems in the context of Indonesian social media.

articleTitle: Solving Unequal Area Facility Layout Problems Using Population-Based Simulated Annealing and Ant Colony Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Facility Layout Design (FLD) is one of the critical factors in the operational success of manufacturing companies as it has a great impact for the efficiency and flexibility of the production systems. The Unequal Area Facility Layout Problems (UA-FLP), problem related to FLD, has been widely studied for its similarity to real-world applications. UA-FLP aims to allocate unequal facilities within layout boundaries while minimising material handling costs and avoiding overlaps. Various heuristic and meta-heuristic approaches have been widely used to solve UA-FLP and have effectively resolved this challenging problem. The goal of this study is to employ a population-based simulated annealing (PSA) approach that has not previously been applied to address UA-FLP. PSA improves standard SA by utilizing a population of candidate solutions, allowing the algorithm to more thoroughly explore the solution space. The study compares the performance of PSA with other methods across five distinct facility layout instances, characterized by varying dimensions and configurations. The results show that PSA has excellent performance in most cases. PSA managed to outperform ACO in all instances, achieving lower material handling costs and requiring significantly less computational time, especially in larger datasets. PSA also shows excellent performance in small and medium instances compared to PSO and DE, although it ranks third behind DE and PSO in the largest instances. These findings suggest that PSA is a promising approach for solving UA-FLP and could inform future advancements in optimization solutions for complex facility layout challenges.

articleTitle: Optimizing Heavy Metal Detection with Deep Neural Networks and Gaussian Mixture Clustering in Voltammetric Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The accurate and efficient detection of heavy metal is of paramount importance, given their deleterious effects on human health and the environment. While traditional laboratory methods are highly accurate, they are not without challenges, including high cost, non-portability, and time-consuming procedures. This study introduces a novel framework that integrates deep learning and clustering techniques to enhance the detection and classification of heavy metal from voltammetric data. The data were collected using cyclic voltammetry (CV) methods with a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) and subsequently analyzed using five classifiers. The following classifiers were employed: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), XGBoost, and Deep Neural Networks (DNN). A dataset comprising 750 samples, categorized into three groups (cadmium, non-heavy metal, and lead), was subjected to advanced preprocessing techniques, including data normalization and dimensionality reduction through principal component analysis (PCA). The DNN model demonstrated superior accuracy, achieving 99.87%. This highlights its capacity to process noisy and complex data more effectively than traditional methods. Additionally, Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) were employed to cluster and identify anomalies within the data. Despite its high accuracy, this study discusses limitations such as computational complexity and potential challenges in highly contaminated environments. These results underscore the significance of developing portable, efficient detection systems for on-site applications, offering a notable advancement over traditional techniques.

articleTitle: Analyzing Overtourism Dynamics in Bali: A Data-Driven Approach Using Geospatial Analysis and Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Overtourism is a growing global challenge, particularly in destinations where tourism volumes exceed sustainable limits, leading to overcrowding and environmental strain. Bali, a leading global tourist destination, faces significant pressures in its southern regions. This study investigates the relationship between infrastructure density and perceived overcrowding in Bali by integrating binary text classification and geospatial analysis. A fine-tuned BERT-based model categorizes tourist reviews as “crowded” or “not crowded” to extract perceptions of congestion, while Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) maps infrastructure concentration and identifies overcrowding hotspots. The findings reveal a moderate positive correlation between infrastructure density and perceived overcrowding, emphasizing the impact of tourism infrastructure on visitor dissatisfaction. This study advocates for decentralizing infrastructure to underdeveloped regions and improving visitor flow management during peak seasons to address overtourism. The results provide actionable insights for policymakers, offering a framework to guide sustainable tourism strategies and preserve Bali's cultural and environmental integrity.

articleTitle: Classification of Cervical Precancerous Cells Using Gabor Filter and Haar Wavelet Features Based on Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health concern, particularly in low-resource regions. This study explored the classification of cervical precancerous cell images using texture-based feature extraction and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). Gabor Filter and Haar Wavelet Transform were applied to extract critical morphological and textural features, which were classified using Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs) trained with One Step Secant (OSS) and Gradient Descent with Momentum and Adaptive Learning Rate Backpropagation (GDX) algorithms. The best performance was achieved using Haar Wavelet features with OSS-MLP, attaining a training accuracy of 79.3% with 15 hidden neurons. Evaluation through Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves demonstrated OSS-MLP's capability to leverage texture features for classification. This research emphasizes the potential of integrating advanced feature extraction with optimized neural networks to develop a reliable and automated diagnostic system for cervical cancer, providing a promising solution for efficient and accurate screening.

articleTitle: Weather Prediction Using Cross-Visual Data with Random Forest and LSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The climate crisis that has occurred in recent decades has led to significant environmental changes, including increasing temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and increasingly frequent extreme weather events. These changes have a direct impact on various sectors, especially the agricultural sector, which is the main foundation for food provision. Big data analysis is emerging as an innovative solution to analyze and predict weather conditions by utilizing historical data such as temperature, humadity, cloud cover, sea level preasure, wind speed and rainfall. This analysis can provide important insights in making decisions on sustainable agricultural strategies, especially in determining the early planting period to minimize the risk of crop failure and ensure food security in the future. This study aims to implement the weather prediction system using machine learning methods, comparing random forests and short-term memory algorithms (LSTM). The system development process includes several stages, namely Data Collection, Preprocessing, Model Training, and Testing using 136,800 datasets from 38 provinces in Indonesia in the last 10 years from BMKG, BPS, and visual cross data website. The comparison results show that the LSTM method performs better, with a difference of 1.16% compared to the Random Forest method, with a Mean Absolute Error value of 0.0345. This prediction system will help farmers determine the optimal planting time according to dynamic climate conditions.

articleTitle: EfficientNet-B0 and YOLOv8 Models with Adam Optimizer for Rice Leaf Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Rice leaf diseases significantly threaten agricultural productivity, necessitating timely and accurate detection to prevent crop loss. This paper presents a dual-model approach for classifying rice leaf diseases using EfficientNet-B0 and YOLOv8 deep learning models optimized with the Adam optimizer. The models were trained on high-resolution images to classify four common rice leaf diseases—bacterial blight, blast, brown spot, and tungro. Data preprocessing, including resizing, rescaling, and data augmentation, was applied to enhance model generalization. EfficientNet-B0 achieved an accuracy of 99%, while YOLOv8 reached 97.5%, with EfficientNet-B0 outperforming YOLOv8 in precision, recall, and F1 scores across all disease categories. These results demonstrate that the proposed system is highly effective in classifying rice leaf diseases, offering both high accuracy and real-time detection capabilities, contributing to the development of automated tools for precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Discrete Wavelet Transform for Age Estimation in Human Face Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: Age estimation from human facial images is a critical research area in computer vision, with applications in security, healthcare, and personalized services. Existing methods often face challenges in balancing accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness against variations in facial features and conditions. This study addresses these issues by leveraging Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) as a lightweight feature extraction technique to capture age-relevant patterns from facial images. Using these features, multiple machines learning models, including Decision Trees, Random Forest, SVM, and Ensemble Methods (Boosting, Bagging, Voting, Stacking), were evaluated. Results indicate that the Boosting Ensemble Model achieved the best performance, with the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 9.16, Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 162.66, and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 12.75, owing to its iterative refinement of weak learners and effective use of DWT-extracted features. This study demonstrates the potential of combining DWT and Boosting for lightweight, accurate, and scalable age estimation systems, offering a robust solution for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Optimization for Transformer-Based Translation Models on Low-Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The limited English proficiency in Indonesia, ranked 79th globally according to the English Proficiency Index (EPI), creates significant barriers in accessing global opportunities across education, business, and technology. Machine Translation (MT), particularly Neural Machine Translation (NMT), has emerged as a promising solution to overcome such linguistic challenges. This study explores the impact of hyperparameter optimization on translation accuracy in models deployed on edge devices, such as the Raspberry Pi Zero, which have limited computational power and memory. A Transformer-based NMT model was developed and trained using the Tatoeba dataset, consisting of English-Indonesian sentence pairs. The primary focus was on optimizing four key hyperparameters: the number of layers (num_layers), model dimension (d_model), feed-forward dimension (dff), and the number of attention heads (num_heads). Eight different scenarios were designed to evaluate how variations in these hyperparameters affect both the model's translation accuracy, measured by the BLEU score, and the execution time on the edge device. The results reveal a trade-off between model accuracy and execution time. While higher values of num_layers, d_model, and num_heads led to improved BLEU scores, they also significantly increased the execution time, sometimes making the model impractical for real-time applications on devices with limited resources. Conversely, configurations with lower hyperparameter values were more efficient in terms of execution time but at the cost of reduced translation accuracy. The findings underscore the importance of carefully balancing hyperparameter settings to achieve a model that is both accurate and efficient on edge devices. This study provides valuable insights for developers aiming to deploy deep learning models on low-power hardware, emphasizing the need for strategic hyperparameter optimization in such constrained environments.

articleTitle: Empowering the Capabilities and Service Optimization for Location Tracking and Management of School Bus Passenger Density in Jakarta Through the Integration of CV-AI
publicationTitle: 2024 Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference (BTS-I2C)
abstract: The school public transportation mobile application is a mobile application that creates safe and secure school bus transportation. It has a real-time bus tracking location and notification to the parents while the student boards the bus. However, the lack of appropriate information in the mobile application leads to significant challenges for students in crowded cities, such as prolonged waiting times due to the absence of real-time information about bus capacity and bus arrivals at transit stations.
